summary_brief: 2026年4月15日，AI Agent生态出现历史首次全4语言SDK（Sonnet/Opus 4）同步废弃宣告，标志着Anthropic模型代际切换正式启动。同时，插件市场从"平台级接入"（4月14日 Salesforce/Azure/Shopify）向垂直领域深度延伸——Shopify电商套件和Bigdata金融分析插件同日进入官方市场，形成有史以来最大规模垂直生态扩张。安全能力今日完成从"协同修复"（4月初）→"系统性审计"（4月中旬）→"架构级默认配置"（今日 gptme 沙箱+输入验证+SSRF防护）的第三阶段质变。OpenClaw生态连续第五日高度活跃（200 commits），从架构重构转入安全与记忆双主线。上下文管理延续4月9日以来的演进链，今日新增上下文压缩和1小时Prompt缓存TTL，Token效率优化进入精细化阶段。信号密度26个（高影响8个），属4月正常水平，远低于3月31日历史峰值（77个），生态进入稳态成熟期而非新一轮爆发。

# 🚀 Release `autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.55`

**Date:** april 2026

---

## 🔥 What's New?

### New Features
- **#12720** - Add Graphiti temporal knowledge graph memory for CoPilot (by @ntindle)

- **#12747** - Upgrade claude-agent-sdk to 0.1.58 with OpenRouter compatibility and cost controls (by @majdyz)
- **#12787** - Add for_agent_generation flag to find_block in CoPilot (by @majdyz)
- **#12786** - Standard/advanced model toggle with Opus rate-limit multiplier (by @majdyz)
- **#12757** - Enhance cost dashboard with token breakdown and averages in platform admin (by @majdyz)

- **#12758** - Enable cross-user prompt caching via SystemPromptPreset (by @majdyz)
- **#12790** - Make system prompt fully static for cross-user prompt caching (by @majdyz)

### UI/UX Improvements
- **#12793** - Align ModelToggleButton styling and add execution ID filter to platform cost page (by @majdyz)
- **#12792** - Load older chat messages reliably and preserve scrollback across turns (by @kcze)
- **#12770** - Tighten artifact preview behavior (by @ntindle)

### Bug Fixes
- **#12636** - P0 guardrails, transient retry, and security hardening in CoPilot (by @majdyz)
- **#12718** - Unify CoPilot auth headers and propagate impersonation header (by @majdyz)
- **#12759** - Deduplicate SSE-replayed messages by content fingerprint (by @majdyz)
- **#12763** - Strip `<internal_reasoning>` tags from Sonnet response stream (by @majdyz)
- **#12739** - Keep credential setup inline on run and schedule paths (by @majdyz)
- **#12768** - Remove extra blank line in platform_cost_test.py (by @Bentlybro)
- **#12777** - Fix T2+ --resume by using CLI native session file (by @majdyz)
- **#12774** - Fix sub-agent session hang and orphan on E2B API stall (by @majdyz)
- **#12761** - Store mode per session so indicator updates on switch (by @majdyz)
- **#12750** - Unified MCP file tools (Read/Write/Edit) to prevent truncation data loss (by @majdyz)
- **#12762** - Baseline cost tracking and cache token display (by @majdyz)
- **#12782** - Robust context fallback — upload gate, gap-fill, and token-budget compression (by @majdyz)
- **#12735** - Charge per LLM iteration and per tool call in OrchestratorBlock (by @majdyz)
- **#12789** - Null-safe token accumulation for OpenRouter null cache fields (by @majdyz)
- **#12766** - Abort SSE stream and disconnect backend listeners on session switch (by @0ubbe)
- **#12788** - Idempotency guard and frontend dedup fix for duplicate messages (by @majdyz)
- **#12795** - Set session_id on mode-switch T1 to enable --resume on subsequent SDK turns (by @majdyz)

### Documentation
- **#12695** - Add coverage guidance to pr-address skill (by @Otto-AGPT)

### Dependencies & Maintenance
- **#12682** - Add Playwright PR smoke suite with seeded QA accounts (by @Abhi1992002)
- **#12778** - Untrack auto-generated API client model files (by @majdyz)

---

## 🎉 Thanks to Our Contributors!

As well as our returning contributors:
- @majdyz
- @0ubbe
- @kcze
- @ntindle
- @Bentlybro
- @Abhi1992002
- @Otto-AGPT

---

## 📥 How to Get This Update

To update to this version, run:

```bash
git pull origin autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.55
```

Or download it directly from the  
[Releases page](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/releases).

For a complete list of changes, see the [Full Changelog](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/compare/autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.54...autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.55).

releases.summary:
## New Features
- Added `codex marketplace add` and app-server support for installing plugin marketplaces from GitHub, git URLs, local directories, and direct `marketplace.json` URLs (#17087, #17717, #17756).
- Added TUI prompt history improvements, including `Ctrl+R` reverse search and local recall for accepted slash commands (#17550, #17336).
- Added TUI and app-server controls for memory mode, memory reset/deletion, and memory-extension cleanup (#17632, #17626, #17913, #17937, #17844).
- Expanded MCP/plugin support with MCP Apps tool calls, namespaced MCP registration, parallel-call opt-in, and sandbox-state metadata for MCP servers (#17364, #17404, #17667, #17763).
- Added realtime and app-server APIs for output modality, transcript completion events, raw turn item injection, and symlink-aware filesystem metadata (#17701, #17703, #17719).
- Added a secure devcontainer profile with bubblewrap support, plus macOS sandbox allowlists for Unix sockets (#10431, #17547, #17654).

## Bug Fixes
- Fixed macOS sandbox/proxy handling for private DNS and removed the `danger-full-access` denylist-only network mode (#17370, #17732).
- Fixed Windows cwd/session matching so `resume --last` and `thread/list` work when paths use verbatim prefixes (#17414).
- Fixed rate-limit/account handling for `prolite` plans and made unknown WHAM plan values decodable (#17419).
- Made Guardian timeouts distinct from policy denials, with timeout-specific guidance and visible TUI history entries (#17381, #17486, #17521, #17557).
- Stabilized app-server behavior by avoiding premature thread unloads, tolerating failed trust persistence on startup, and skipping broken symlinks in `fs/readDirectory` (#17398, #17595, #17907).
- Fixed MCP/tool-call edge cases including flattened deferred tool names, elicitation timeout accounting, and empty namespace descriptions (#17556, #17566, #17946).

## Documentation
- Documented the secure devcontainer profile and its bubblewrap requirements (#10431, #17547).
- Added TUI composer documentation for history search behavior (#17550).
- Updated app-server docs for new MCP, marketplace, turn injection, memory reset, filesystem metadata, external-agent migration, and websocket token-hash APIs (#17364, #17717, #17703, #17913, #17719, #17855, #17871).
- Documented WSL1 bubblewrap limitations and WSL2 behavior (#17559).
- Added memory pipeline documentation for extension cleanup (#17844).

## Chores
- Hardened supply-chain and CI inputs by pinning GitHub Actions, cargo installs, git dependencies, V8 checksums, and cargo-deny source allowlists (#17471).
- Added Bazel release-build verification so release-only Rust code is compiled in PR CI (#17704, #17705).
- Introduced the `codex-thread-store` crate/interface and moved local thread listing behind it (#17659, #17824).
- Required reviewed pnpm dependency build scripts for workspace installs (#17558).
- Reduced Rust maintenance surface with broader absolute-path types and removal of unused helper APIs (#17407, #17792, #17146).

releases.author: sdcoffey
releases.summary:
## What's Changed

### Sandbox Agents

This release adds **Sandbox Agents**, a beta SDK surface for running agents with a persistent, isolated workspace. Sandbox agents keep the normal `Agent` and `Runner` flow, but add workspace manifests, sandbox-native capabilities, sandbox clients, snapshots, and resume support so agents can work over real files, run commands, edit repositories, generate artifacts, and continue work across runs.

Key pieces:

- `SandboxAgent`: an `Agent` with sandbox defaults such as `default_manifest`, sandbox instructions, capabilities, and `run_as`.
- `Manifest`: a fresh-workspace contract for files, directories, local files, local directories, Git repos, environment, users, groups, and mounts.
- `SandboxRunConfig`: per-run sandbox wiring for client creation, live session injection, serialized session resume, manifest overrides, snapshots, and materialization concurrency limits.
- Built-in capabilities for shell access, filesystem editing and image inspection, skills, memory, and compaction.
- Workspace snapshots and serialized sandbox session state for reconnecting to existing work or seeding a fresh sandbox from saved contents.

### Sandbox clients and hosted providers

Sandbox agents now support local, containerized, and hosted execution backends:

- `UnixLocalSandboxClient` for fast local development.
- `DockerSandboxClient` for container isolation and image parity.
- Hosted sandbox clients for Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Runloop, and Vercel through optional extras.

The release also adds provider-specific examples and mount strategies for common storage backends, including S3, Cloudflare R2, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and S3 Files where supported by the selected backend.

### Sandbox memory

Adds a sandbox memory capability that lets future sandbox-agent runs learn from prior runs. Memory stores extracted lessons in the sandbox workspace, injects a concise summary into later runs, and uses progressive disclosure so agents can search deeper rollout summaries only when useful.

Memory supports:

- Read-only or generate-only modes.
- Live updates when the agent discovers stale memory.
- Multi-turn grouping through `conversation_id`, SDK `Session`, `RunConfig.group_id`, or generated run IDs.
- Separate memory layouts for isolating memory across agents or workflows.
- S3-backed examples for persisted memory across runs.

### Workspace mounts, snapshots, and resume

This release adds a full workspace entry and mount model for sandbox sessions:

- Local files and directories.
- Synthetic files and directories.
- Git repository entries.
- Remote storage mounts for S3, R2, GCS, Azure Blob Storage, and S3 Files.
- Provider-specific mount strategies across Docker, Modal, Cloudflare, Blaxel, Daytona, E2B, and Runloop.
- Portable snapshots with path normalization, symlink preservation, mount-safe snapshotting, and remote snapshot support.
- Resume paths through runner-managed `RunState`, explicit `SandboxSessionState`, or saved snapshots.

### Examples and tutorials

Adds a large `examples/sandbox/` suite covering:

- Local Unix and Docker sandbox runners.
- Docker mount smoke tests for S3, GCS, Azure Blob Storage, and S3 Files.
- Sandbox coding tasks with skills.
- Sandbox agents as tools and handoff patterns.
- Memory examples, including multi-agent/multi-turn memory and S3-backed memory.
- Tax-prep and healthcare-support workflows.
- Dataroom QA and metric extraction tutorials.
- Repository code review tutorial.
- Vision website clone tutorial.
- Provider examples for Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Runloop, Temporal, and Vercel.

### Runtime, tracing, and model plumbing

The release includes the runtime plumbing needed to make sandbox agents work naturally inside the existing SDK:

- Runner-managed sandbox preparation, capability binding, session lifecycle, state serialization, and resume behavior.
- Sandbox-aware `RunState` serialization.
- Unified sandbox tracing with SDK spans.
- Token usage on tracing spans.
- Runner-managed prompt cache key defaults.
- OpenAI agent registration and harness ID configuration.
- Safer redaction of sensitive MCP tool outputs when sensitive tracing is disabled.
- Additional OpenAI client/model utilities and Chat Completions coverage.


## Documentation & Other Changes

- docs: add Asqav to external tracing processors list.
- docs: update translated document pages.

releases.author: ashwin-ant
releases.summary:
## What's changed

- Added `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` env var to opt into 1-hour prompt cache TTL on API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry (`ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H_BEDROCK` is deprecated but still honored), and `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` to force 5-minute TTL
- Added recap feature to provide context when returning to a session, configurable in /config and manually invocable with /recap; force with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY` if telemetry disabled.
- The model can now discover and invoke built-in slash commands like `/init`, `/review`, and `/security-review` via the Skill tool
- `/undo` is now an alias for `/rewind`
- Improved `/model` to warn before switching models mid-conversation, since the next response re-reads the full history uncached
- Improved `/resume` picker to default to sessions from the current directory; press `Ctrl+A` to show all projects
- Improved error messages: server rate limits are now distinguished from plan usage limits; 5xx/529 errors show a link to status.claude.com; unknown slash commands suggest the closest match
- Reduced memory footprint for file reads, edits, and syntax highlighting by loading language grammars on demand
- Added "verbose" indicator when viewing the detailed transcript (`Ctrl+O`)
- Added a warning at startup when prompt caching is disabled via `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING*` environment variables
- Fixed paste not working in the `/login` code prompt (regression in 2.1.105)
- Fixed subscribers who set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` falling back to 5-minute prompt cache TTL instead of 1 hour
- Fixed Agent tool prompting for permission in auto mode when the safety classifier's transcript exceeded its context window
- Fixed Bash tool producing no output when `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` (e.g. `~/.zprofile`) ends with a `#` comment line
- Fixed `claude --resume <session-id>` losing the session's custom name and color set via `/rename`
- Fixed session titles showing placeholder example text when the first message is a short greeting
- Fixed terminal escape codes appearing as garbage text in the prompt input after `--teleport`
- Fixed `/feedback` retry: pressing Enter to resubmit after a failure now works without first editing the description
- Fixed `--teleport` and `--resume <id>` precondition errors (e.g. dirty git tree, session not found) exiting silently instead of showing the error message
- Fixed Remote Control session titles set in the web UI being overwritten by auto-generated titles after the third message
- Fixed `--resume` truncating sessions when the transcript contained a self-referencing message
- Fixed transcript write failures (e.g., disk full) being silently dropped instead of being logged
- Fixed diacritical marks (accents, umlauts, cedillas) being dropped from responses when the `language` setting is configured
- Fixed policy-managed plugins never auto-updating when running from a different project than where they were first installed

key_changes: 新增 recap 功能：会话返回时可获取上下文摘要，支持手动调用 /recap 和环境变量强制开启
Skill 工具可调用内置斜杠命令（如 /init、/review、/security-review）
新增 ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H 环境变量支持 1 小时 prompt 缓存 TTL
内存优化：语言语法文件改为按需加载，降低文件读取和语法高亮的内存占用
错误提示改进：区分服务器限流与计划配额限制，5xx 错误增加状态页面链接
ai_summary.summary_cn: 本次更新增强了会话恢复和上下文管理能力，recap 功能让用户返回会话时能快速了解之前进展。模型现在可以直接调用内置斜杠命令，配合按需加载的语法文件优化了资源使用。修复了登录界面粘贴失效、Bash 工具在配置文件以 # 结尾时无输出等多个 bug。

releases.author: vincentkoc
releases.summary:
OpenClaw `2026.4.14` is another broad quality release focused on model provider with explicit turn improvements for GPT-5 family and channel provider issues. Additionally we improved overal performance with refactors to our underlying core codebase.

## Changes

- OpenAI Codex/models: add forward-compat support for `gpt-5.4-pro`, including Codex pricing/limits and list/status visibility before the upstream catalog catches up. (#66453) Thanks @jepson-liu.
- Telegram/forum topics: surface human topic names in agent context, prompt metadata, and plugin hook metadata by learning names from Telegram forum service messages. (#65973) Thanks @ptahdunbar.

## Fixes

- Agents/Ollama: forward the configured embedded-run timeout into the global undici stream timeout tuning so slow local Ollama runs no longer inherit the default stream cutoff instead of the operator-set run timeout. (#63175) Thanks @mindcraftreader and @vincentkoc.
- Models/Codex: include `apiKey` in the codex provider catalog output so the Pi ModelRegistry validator no longer rejects the entry and silently drops all custom models from every provider in `models.json`. (#66180) Thanks @hoyyeva.
- Tools/image+pdf: normalize configured provider/model refs before media-tool registry lookup so image and PDF tool runs stop rejecting valid Ollama vision models as unknown just because the tool path skipped the usual model-ref normalization step. (#59943) Thanks @yqli2420 and @vincentkoc.
- Slack/interactions: apply the configured global `allowFrom` owner allowlist to channel block-action and modal interactive events, require an expected sender id for cross-verification, and reject ambiguous channel types so interactive triggers can no longer bypass the documented allowlist intent in channels without a `users` list. Open-by-default behavior is preserved when no allowlists are configured. (#66028) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Media-understanding/attachments: fail closed when a local attachment path cannot be canonically resolved via `realpath`, so a `realpath` error can no longer downgrade the canonical-roots allowlist check to a non-canonical comparison; attachments that also have a URL still fall back to the network fetch path. (#66022) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Agents/gateway-tool: reject `config.patch` and `config.apply` calls from the model-facing gateway tool when they would newly enable any flag enumerated by `openclaw security audit` (for example `dangerouslyDisableDeviceAuth`, `allowInsecureAuth`, `dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, `hooks.gmail.allowUnsafeExternalContent`, `tools.exec.applyPatch.workspaceOnly: false`); already-enabled flags pass through unchanged so non-dangerous edits in the same patch still apply, and direct authenticated operator RPC behavior is unchanged. (#62006) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Google image generation: strip a trailing `/openai` suffix from configured Google base URLs only when calling the native Gemini image API so Gemini image requests stop 404ing without breaking explicit OpenAI-compatible Google endpoints. (#66445) Thanks @dapzthelegend.
- Telegram/forum topics: persist learned topic names to the Telegram session sidecar store so agent context can keep using human topic names after a restart instead of relearning from future service metadata. (#66107) Thanks @obviyus.
- Doctor/systemd: keep `openclaw doctor --repair` and service reinstall from re-embedding dotenv-backed secrets in user systemd units, while preserving newer inline overrides over stale state-dir `.env` values. (#66249) Thanks @tmimmanuel.
- Ollama/OpenAI-compat: send `stream_options.include_usage` for Ollama streaming completions so local Ollama runs report real usage instead of falling back to bogus prompt-token counts that trigger premature compaction. (#64568) Thanks @xchunzhao and @vincentkoc.
- Doctor/plugins: cache external `preferOver` catalog lookups within each plugin auto-enable pass so large `agents.list` configs no longer peg CPU and repeatedly reread plugin catalogs during doctor/plugins resolution. (#66246) Thanks @yfge.
- GitHub Copilot/thinking: allow `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` to use `xhigh` reasoning so Copilot GPT-5.4 matches the rest of the GPT-5.4 family. (#50168) Thanks @jakepresent and @vincentkoc.
- Memory/embeddings: preserve non-OpenAI provider prefixes when normalizing OpenAI-compatible embedding model refs so proxy-backed memory providers stop failing with `Unknown memory embedding provider`. (#66452) Thanks @jlapenna.
- Agents/local models: clarify low-context preflight hints for self-hosted models, point config-backed caps at the relevant OpenClaw setting, and stop suggesting larger models when `agents.defaults.contextTokens` is the real limit. (#66236) Thanks @ImLukeF.
- Browser/SSRF: restore hostname navigation under the default browser SSRF policy while keeping explicit strict mode reachable from config, and keep managed loopback CDP `/json/new` fallback requests on the local CDP control policy so browser follow-up fixes stop regressing normal navigation or self-blocking local CDP control. (#66386) Thanks @obviyus.
- Models/Codex: canonicalize the legacy `openai-codex/gpt-5.4-codex` runtime alias to `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` while still honoring alias-specific and canonical per-model overrides. (#43060) Thanks @Sapientropic and @vincentkoc.
- Browser/SSRF: preserve explicit strict browser navigation mode for legacy `browser.ssrfPolicy.allowPrivateNetwork: false` configs by normalizing the legacy alias to the canonical strict marker instead of silently widening those installs to the default non-strict hostname-navigation path.
- Onboarding/custom providers: use `max_tokens=16` for OpenAI-compatible verification probes so stricter custom endpoints stop rejecting onboarding checks that only need a tiny completion. (#66450) Thanks @WuKongAI-CMU.
- Agents/subagents: emit the subagent registry lazy-runtime stub on the stable dist path that both source and bundled runtime imports resolve, so the follow-up dist fix no longer still fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at runtime. (#66420) Thanks @obviyus.
- Media-understanding/proxy env: auto-upgrade provider HTTP helper requests to trusted env-proxy mode only when `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` is active and the target is not bypassed by `NO_PROXY`, so remote media-understanding and transcription requests stop failing local DNS pre-resolution in proxy-only environments without widening SSRF bypasses. (#52162) Thanks @mjamiv and @vincentkoc.
- Telegram/media downloads: let Telegram media fetches trust an operator-configured explicit proxy for target DNS resolution after hostname-policy checks, so proxy-backed installs stop failing `could not download media` on Bot API file downloads after the DNS-pinning regression. (#66245) Thanks @dawei41468 and @vincentkoc.
- Browser: keep loopback CDP readiness checks reachable under strict SSRF defaults so OpenClaw can reconnect to locally started managed Chrome. (#66354) Thanks @hxy91819.
- Agents/context engine: compact engine-owned sessions from the first tool-loop delta and preserve ingest fallback when `afterTurn` is absent, so long-running tool loops can stay bounded without dropping engine state. (#63555) Thanks @Bikkies.
- OpenAI Codex/auth: keep malformed Codex CLI auth-file diagnostics on the debug logger instead of stdout so interactive command output stays clean while auth read failures remain traceable. (#66451) Thanks @SimbaKingjoe.
- Discord/native commands: return the real status card for native `/status` interactions instead of falling through to the synthetic `✅ Done.` ack when the generic dispatcher produces no visible reply. (#54629) Thanks @tkozzer and @vincentkoc.
- Hooks/Ollama: let LLM-backed session-memory slug generation honor an explicit `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` override instead of always aborting after 15 seconds, so slow local Ollama runs stop silently dropping back to generic filenames. (#66237) Thanks @dmak and @vincentkoc.
- Media/transcription: remap `.aac` filenames to `.m4a` for OpenAI-compatible audio uploads so AAC voice notes stop failing MIME-sensitive transcription endpoints. (#66446) Thanks @ben-z.
- UI/chat: replace marked.js with markdown-it so maliciously crafted markdown can no longer freeze the Control UI via ReDoS. (#46707) Thanks @zhangfnf.
- Auto-reply/send policy: keep `sendPolicy: "deny"` from blocking inbound message processing, so the agent still runs its turn while all outbound delivery is suppressed for observer-style setups. (#65461, #53328) Thanks @omarshahine.
- BlueBubbles: lazy-refresh the Private API server-info cache on send when reply threading or message effects are requested but status is unknown, so sends no longer silently degrade to plain messages when the 10-minute cache expires. (#65447, #43764) Thanks @omarshahine.
- Heartbeat/security: force owner downgrade for untrusted `hook:wake` system events [AI-assisted]. (#66031) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Browser/security: enforce SSRF policy on snapshot, screenshot, and tab routes [AI]. (#66040) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Microsoft Teams/security: enforce sender allowlist checks on SSO signin invokes [AI]. (#66033) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Config/security: redact `sourceConfig` and `runtimeConfig` alias fields in `redactConfigSnapshot` [AI]. (#66030) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Agents/context engines: run opt-in turn maintenance as idle-aware background work so the next foreground turn no longer waits on proactive maintenance. (#65233) Thanks @100yenadmin.
- Plugins/status: report the registered context-engine IDs in `plugins inspect` instead of the owning plugin ID, so non-matching engine IDs and multi-engine plugins are classified correctly. (#58766) Thanks @zhuisDEV.
- Context engines: reject resolved plugin engines whose reported `info.id` does not match their registered slot id, so malformed engines fail fast before id-based runtime branches can misbehave. (#63222) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- WhatsApp: patch installed Baileys media encryption writes during OpenClaw postinstall so the default npm/install.sh delivery path waits for encrypted media files to finish flushing before readback, avoiding transient `ENOENT` crashes on image sends. (#65896) Thanks @frankekn.
- Gateway/update: unify service entrypoint resolution around the canonical bundled gateway entrypoint so update, reinstall, and doctor repair stop drifting between stale `dist/entry.js` and current `dist/index.js` paths. (#65984) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Heartbeat/Telegram topics: keep isolated heartbeat replies on the bound forum topic when `target=last`, instead of dropping them into the group root chat. (#66035) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Browser/CDP: let managed local Chrome readiness, status probes, and managed loopback CDP control bypass browser SSRF policy for their own loopback control plane, so OpenClaw no longer misclassifies a healthy child browser as "not reachable after start". (#65695, #66043) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Gateway/sessions: stop heartbeat, cron-event, and exec-event turns from overwriting shared-session routing and origin metadata, preventing synthetic `heartbeat` targets from poisoning later cron or user delivery. (#66073, #63733, #35300) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Browser/CDP: let local attach-only `manual-cdp` profiles reuse the local loopback CDP control plane under strict default policy and remote-class probe timeouts, so tabs/snapshot stop falsely reporting a live local browser session as not running. (#65611, #66080) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Cron/scheduler: stop inventing short retries when cron next-run calculation returns no valid future slot, and keep a maintenance wake armed so enabled unscheduled jobs recover without entering a refire loop. (#66019, #66083) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Cron/scheduler: preserve the active error-backoff floor when maintenance repair recomputes a missing cron next-run, so recurring errored jobs do not resume early after a transient next-run resolution failure. (#66019, #66083, #66113) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Outbound/delivery-queue: persist the originating outbound `session` context on queued delivery entries and replay it during recovery, so write-ahead-queued sends keep their original outbound media policy context after restart instead of evaluating against a missing session. (#66025) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Memory/Ollama: restore the built-in `ollama` embedding adapter in memory-core so explicit `memorySearch.provider: "ollama"` works again, and include endpoint-aware cache keys so different Ollama hosts do not reuse each other's embeddings. (#63429, #66078, #66163) Thanks @nnish16 and @vincentkoc.
- Auto-reply/queue: split collect-mode followup drains into contiguous groups by per-message authorization context (sender id, owner status, exec/bash-elevated overrides), so queued items from different senders or exec configs no longer execute under the last queued run's owner-only and exec-approval context. (#66024) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Dreaming/memory-core: require a live queued Dreaming cron event before the heartbeat hook runs the sweep, so managed Dreaming no longer replays on later heartbeats after the scheduled run was already consumed. (#66139) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Control UI/Dreaming: stop Imported Insights and Memory Palace from calling optional `memory-wiki` gateway methods when the plugin is off, and refresh config before wiki reloads so the Dreaming tab stops showing misleading unknown-method failures. (#66140) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Agents/tools: only mark streamed unknown-tool retries as counted when a streamed message actually classifies an unavailable tool, and keep incomplete streamed tool names from resetting the retry streak before the final assistant message arrives. (#66145) Thanks @dutifulbob.
- Memory/active-memory: move recalled memory onto the hidden untrusted prompt-prefix path instead of system prompt injection, label the visible Active Memory status line fields, and include the resolved recall provider/model in gateway debug logs so trace/debug output matches what the model actually saw. (#66144) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- Memory/QMD: stop treating legacy lowercase `memory.md` as a second default root collection, so QMD recall no longer searches phantom `memory-alt-*` collections and builtin/QMD root-memory fallback stays aligned. (#66141) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Agents/subagents: ship `dist/agents/subagent-registry.runtime.js` in npm builds so `runtime: "subagent"` runs stop stalling in `queued` after the registry import fails. (#66189) Thanks @yqli2420 and @vincentkoc.
- Agents/OpenAI: map `minimal` thinking to OpenAI's supported `low` reasoning effort for GPT-5.4 requests, so embedded runs stop failing request validation. Thanks @steipete.
- Voice-call/media-stream: resolve the source IP from trusted forwarding headers for per-IP pending-connection limits when `webhookSecurity.trustForwardingHeaders` and `trustedProxyIPs` are configured, and reserve `maxConnections` capacity for in-flight WebSocket upgrades so concurrent handshakes can no longer momentarily exceed the operator-set cap. (#66027) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Feishu/allowlist: canonicalize allowlist entries by explicit `user`/`chat` kind, strip repeated `feishu:`/`lark:` provider prefixes, and stop folding opaque Feishu IDs to lowercase, so allowlist matching no longer crosses user/chat namespaces or widens to case-insensitive ID matches the operator did not intend. (#66021) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Telegram/status commands: let read-only status slash commands bypass busy topic turns, while keeping `/export-session` on the normal lane so it cannot interleave with an in-flight session mutation. (#66226) Thanks @VACInc and @vincentkoc.
- TTS/reply media: persist OpenClaw temp voice outputs into managed outbound media and allow them through reply-media normalization, so voice-note replies stop silently dropping. (#63511) Thanks @jetd1.
- Agents/tools: treat Windows drive-letter paths (`C:\\...`) as absolute when resolving sandbox and read-tool paths so workspace root is not prepended under POSIX path rules. (#54039) Thanks @ly85206559 and @vincentkoc.
- Agents/OpenAI: recover embedded GPT-style runs when reasoning-only or empty turns need bounded continuation, with replay-safe retry gating and incomplete-turn fallback when no visible answer arrives. (#66167) thanks @jalehman
- Outbound/relay-status: suppress internal relay-status placeholder payloads (`No channel reply.`, `Replied in-thread.`, `Replied in #...`, wiki-update status variants ending in `No channel reply.`) before channel delivery so internal housekeeping text does not leak to users.
- Slack/doctor: add a dedicated doctor-contract sidecar so config warmup paths such as `openclaw cron` no longer fall back to Slack's broader contract surface, which could trigger Slack-related config-read crashes on affected setups. (#63192) Thanks @shhtheonlyperson.
- Hooks/session-memory: pass the resolved agent workspace into gateway `/new` and `/reset` session-memory hooks so reset snapshots stay scoped to the right agent workspace instead of leaking into the default workspace. (#64735) Thanks @suboss87 and @vincentkoc.
- CLI/approvals: raise the default `openclaw approvals get` gateway timeout and report config-load timeouts explicitly, so slow hosts stop showing a misleading `Config unavailable.` note when the approvals snapshot succeeds but the follow-up config RPC needs more time. (#66239) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- Media/store: honor configured agent media limits when saving generated media and persisting outbound reply media, so the store no longer hard-stops those flows at 5 MB before the configured limit applies. (#66229) Thanks @neeravmakwana and @vincentkoc.

## 🚀 ClawX v0.3.9

ClawX - Graphical AI Assistant based on OpenClaw

### 📦 Downloads

Please select the appropriate installer for your operating system and architecture:

#### macOS
- **Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4)**: `ClawX-*-mac-arm64.dmg`
- **Intel (x64)**: `ClawX-*-mac-x64.dmg`

#### Windows
- **Installer (x64)**: `ClawX-*-win-x64.exe`
- **Installer (ARM64)**: `ClawX-*-win-arm64.exe`

#### Linux
- **AppImage (x64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (Universal format, recommended)
- **AppImage (ARM64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-arm64.AppImage`
- **Debian/Ubuntu (x64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-amd64.deb`
- **Debian/Ubuntu (ARM64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-arm64.deb`
- **RPM (x64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-x86_64.rpm`

### 📝 Release Notes

See the auto-generated release notes below for detailed changes.

### ⚠️ Installation Notes

- **macOS**: On first launch, you may see "cannot verify developer". Go to System Preferences → Security & Privacy to allow the app to run
- **Windows**: SmartScreen may block the app. Click "More info" → "Run anyway" to proceed
- **Linux AppImage**: First run `chmod +x ClawX-*.AppImage` to add execute permission. On Ubuntu 22.04 you may also need `sudo apt install libfuse2`; on Ubuntu 24.04 use `sudo apt install libfuse2t64`
- **Linux .deb (Ubuntu 24.04)**: If installation fails due to missing dependencies, use `sudo apt install libgtk-3-0t64 libnotify4t64 libxss1t64` before installing

---

💬 Found an issue? Please submit an [Issue](https://github.com/ValueCell-ai/ClawX/issues)


## What's Changed
* feat(i18n): add Russian (ru) localization support by @AlexZander85 in https://github.com/ValueCell-ai/ClawX/pull/798
* Fix provider API key validation trimming by @ashione in https://github.com/ValueCell-ai/ClawX/pull/810

* support reasoning agentid by accountId or session for cron by @typhigh in https://github.com/ValueCell-ai/ClawX/pull/847

* release v0.3.9 by @su8su in https://github.com/ValueCell-ai/ClawX/pull/854

## New Contributors

issue_insights.summary_brief: 本次汇总覆盖 18 个仓库，共识别出 5 类跨仓库共性问题，以 workflow_runtime 和 startup_crash 类别问题最为突出，涉及 AI Agent 核心流程阻断、安装失败、认证缺失等高优先级缺陷。
global_highlights: 跨仓库 P0 问题集中于 Windows 合并冲突、Windows Defender 安装卡住、WSL/Linux Secret Service 认证缺失、macOS Electron PATH 不完整四类，影响 12-51 个仓库
agno/agno 和 agentscope-ai/agentscope 各含 3-2 个 P0 workflow_runtime bug，并发竞态、SSE 解析崩溃、Agent 无限循环等问题直接阻断核心功能
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python 含 3 个 P0 startup_crash：stdin 关闭导致 MCP 握手失败、100% CPU 死循环、HTTP 429 崩溃摧毁长会话
Claude Code 在区块链场景执行不可逆转账无确认提示（P0 安全问题），OpenCode Desktop UI 闪烁和 Diff 管道导致严重卡顿
PostgreSQL 磁盘监控以物理大小而非实际数据量阻塞写入，model 定价数据过期导致 trace 成本计算错误

source_issues.title: Agent hallucinates unrelated project after completing assigned task
source_issues.evidence: After agent correctly commits and pushes the assigned task, it suddenly creates a 9-item task plan for building a completely unrelated project. Agent picks up phantom tasks from system prompt context after completing the actual task. Happened twice, indicating a systemic issue with task completion detection.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: OpenHands kills its own process on port 8000 during local web deployment
source_issues.evidence: OpenHands checks for available port and frees port 8000 by terminating the process using it. Problem: port 8000 was being used by OpenHands itself, so OpenHands killed its own main process and crashed the entire service. This is a self-destructive bug in port allocation logic.

Reproduces same class of symptom as closed issues #295 and #730. PR #731 removed timeout-based stdin close but client.py still calls transport.end_input() unconditionally.

source_issues.title: mcp_servers + query() fails: 'ProcessTransport is not ready for writing' (closed, unfixed)

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Every normal completion of async for message in query(...) triggers a cross-task cancel scope exit on async-generator finalization, which cancels the caller's task from an unrelated context and pins anyio's _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU loop until the process restarts. Same underlying bug pattern as #454 and #776.

source_issues.title: Agent SDK should handle 429 rate limits gracefully instead of crashing
source_issues.evidence: SDK crashes fatally on 429. Multi-turn autonomous sessions (10+ min of work) destroyed by a single rate limit. On 30k tokens/min rate limit, any agent reading files >10KB reliably crashes within 10-15 min. User loses all accumulated work. Transient, recoverable HTTP errors should be retried with Retry-After delay.

source_issues.title: cpSync fails on symlinked sensitive files
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes 100% reproducibly with 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, symlink' during sensitive-file restore. Also produces cascading tsconfig.json fd leak error. Affects any repo where CLAUDE.md is a symlink (e.g., CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md). No workaround available.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed same root cause: cpSync in restore-config.ts fails because symlink() is called before parent directory exists. Introduced in #1174. Workaround is to pin to v1.0.88. No fix in later versions.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin MCP fails to start when launched by Claude Code (v0.0.6)
source_issues.evidence: MCP server fails silently when launched by Claude Code. Channel process starts and connects to Telegram (confirmed via ps/lsof), but MCP component fails. /telegram:access shows unknown skill. Pairing is inaccessible.

source_issues.title: [Bug] skills update fails on Windows when Node.js path contains spaces
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 用户在默认路径 C:\Program Files\nodejs\ 下执行 npx skills update，命令静默失败，仅输出 '✗ Failed to update <skill-name>'，无错误详情。根本原因：spawnSync 未对 process.execPath 加引号，cmd.exe 在空格处截断路径为 'C:\Program'，子进程 stdio 被设为 inherit/pipe/pipe 导致错误被吞没。

source_issues.evidence: Installation aborts immediately after download with dyld error: Symbol not found _OBJC_CLASS_$_MTLResidencySetDescriptor expected in Metal.framework. Binary is compiled against a newer Metal SDK than available on target macOS versions, preventing the app from even starting.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude Code executed unauthorized rm -rf due to case-insensitive filesystem path resolution
source_issues.evidence: Claude made a typo in a path (WebstormproJects with capital J), then ran rm -rf on that path. On APFS case-insensitive filesystem, the path resolved to ~/WebstormProjects — the real working directory — which was fully deleted. Claude violated its own documented guardrails (NEVER run destructive git commands unless user explicitly requests; check with user before risky actions; measure twice cut once; do not use destructive actions as shortcuts). Entire project directory with uncommitted work and .env files (API keys) permanently lost. Bypassed Trash.

source_issues.title: Multiple concurrent CLI sessions cause auth failure on token refresh (race condition)
source_issues.evidence: User runs 4-7+ concurrent CLI sessions (Claude Max subscriber). After ~8 hours when OAuth access token expires, all sessions race to refresh. With rotating refresh tokens, the first session succeeds and invalidates the token other sessions are trying to use. All other sessions fail with /login prompt simultaneously. Root cause: no file-locking or coordination mechanism for shared ~/.claude/.credentials.json. Also claude setup-token may revoke existing refresh token server-side, causing all sessions to fail after setup.

source_issues.title: StreamableHTTPClientTransport: OAuth token not forwarded to SSE GET request, causing 401 and disconnect
source_issues.evidence: Debug output shows 'Found stored OAuth token' then 'MCP ERROR: Streamable HTTP error: Failed to open SSE stream: Unauthorized'. Verified working via curl with token included. OAuth flow completes and stores token, but _startOrAuthSse() GET request omits Authorization header.

source_issues.title: deleteCredentials throws when keychain entry doesn't exist, cascading clearCredentials errors

source_issues.title: OAuth refresh tokens discarded on access_token rotation and on stale-credential delete

signals.topic: PostgreSQL disk usage monitor blocks writes based on on-disk size, not live data size — no self-healing path
signals.summary: DbDiskUsageMonitor uses pg_total_relation_size to block writes. After data deletion via UPDATE/DELETE (not Phoenix API), dead tuples remain on disk; routine VACUUM does not reclaim space, so writes remain blocked even when the database is mostly empty. The only fix requires manual VACUUM FULL/pg_repack or raising the capacity cap — no self-healing.
signals.review_reason: Primary flow blocking bug: writes are hard-blocked with no self-healing path. Root cause is a semantic mismatch between on-disk size and live data size in PostgreSQL MVCC, making the blocking condition persist indefinitely after data churn even when the database is functionally empty. Users must perform manual operational maintenance (VACUUM FULL/pg_repack) to recover, which is unexpected and disruptive.

signals.topic: macOS unsigned release causes Gatekeeper warnings blocking end-user installation
signals.summary: When macOS code signing certificates are not configured in CI, the Tauri build produces unsigned releases. End users who download and run these binaries encounter macOS Gatekeeper security warnings requiring extra approval steps (right-click → Open, or System Preferences approval), creating significant friction during installation and first-run. A fallback unsigned build unblocks CI but does not resolve the user-facing experience degradation.
signals.review_reason: Issue #2146 explicitly describes user impact: unsigned macOS releases cause Gatekeeper security warnings and require extra user steps to open ('right-click → Open' or System Preferences approval). This is a recurring, documented experience degradation affecting all macOS end users who download/install the binary. While a CI-level fallback exists (#2121), it only unblocks the build pipeline without fixing the user-facing problem. Count=2 because both #2146 and #2118 share the same root cause and together demonstrate this is an ongoing, unresolved issue (one closed with workaround, one still open). P1 (not P0) because the app remains functional once past Gatekeeper, making it a significant UX degradation rather than a full main-flow block.

source_issues.title: ci(tauri): set up Apple Developer secrets to enable macOS code signing
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states 'unsigned releases are a headache for end users (Gatekeeper warnings, extra steps to open)'. Open issue, actively tracked.

source_issues.title: ci(tauri): macOS code signing and notarization not working
source_issues.evidence: Original CI failure with full error output showing certificate import failure: 'failed to import keychain certificate'. Resolved with unsigned fallback, but underlying user-impacting issue persists in #2146.

signals.topic: LLM integration failures — agent produces empty responses and loops indefinitely in Docker, cannot be canceled
signals.summary: When using Docker installation with OpenAI LLM, the agent enters an endless loop producing empty responses. Error 'LLM produced empty response - continuing agent loop' appears and the chat cannot be canceled, blocking the primary use case.
signals.review_reason: Docker + OpenAI users experience an infinite agent loop with empty LLM responses that cannot be canceled. This is a main-flow blocking issue for Docker users — the primary interaction mode is unusable. Error message explicitly shows the loop continuation behavior.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: using docker will be loop chat response
source_issues.evidence: User reports agent produces empty responses and loops indefinitely with 'LLM produced empty response - continuing agent loop'. The session cannot be canceled, blocking the primary workflow on Docker + OpenAI.

signals.topic: tmux session with oversized terminal dimensions (x=1000 y=1000) wastes ~80% CPU in kernel mode
signals.summary: The tmux session created in the sandbox uses a 1000×1000 character terminal grid by default. This causes tmux to spend ~80% of one CPU core in kernel-mode PTY I/O processing even when the session is detached and producing no useful output, creating significant host resource waste.
signals.review_reason: tmux session wastes ~80% of a CPU core in kernel mode due to oversized (1000×1000) default terminal dimensions. This is a clear resource waste issue that affects every OpenHands session, not just a specific use case. The root cause is identified in the source code (bash.py) with a concrete fix available.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: tmux session with x=1000 y=1000 burns CPU in kernel mode doing nothing useful
source_issues.evidence: tmux session created in openhands/runtime/utils/bash.py uses x=1000, y=1000 which causes tmux to spend ~80% of a CPU core in kernel mode processing PTY I/O for a detached session. Every line of output gets terminal-emulated across a massive grid. Suggested fix is x=220, y=50.

signals.summary: Users following the official Quickstart guide for LM Studio still get 'LLM Provider NOT provided' error, even though the LM Studio API works correctly (verified via curl). Both CLI and Docker installation methods are affected, blocking local LLM usage.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot configure local LLM providers (LM Studio) despite following the official documentation and having a working API. Both CLI and Docker deployment methods are affected. This blocks a core use case — running OpenHands with local/custom LLMs — which is a primary selling point for privacy-conscious users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LLM Provider NOT provided with LM Studio
source_issues.evidence: User followed the official Quickstart guide for LM Studio (local LLM) but OpenHands reports 'LLM Provider NOT provided'. LM Studio API works correctly (curl returns JSON). Both CLI and Docker versions affected. This blocks the local LLM use case entirely.

signals.topic: Agent hallucinates and executes unrelated tasks after completing assigned task correctly
signals.summary: After successfully completing an assigned coding task, the agent suddenly begins building an entirely unrelated project. This has occurred multiple times, picking up phantom tasks from system prompt context after the real task was done. The agent appears to lose context of task completion.
signals.review_reason: Agent continues executing unrelated tasks after the assigned task is complete, wasting compute and potentially making unwanted changes to the codebase. This is a main-flow reliability issue — users cannot trust the agent to stop after a task is done, creating risk of unintended modifications and wasted resources.

source_issues.title: Agent hallucinates unrelated project after completing assigned task
source_issues.evidence: After agent correctly commits and pushes the assigned task, it suddenly creates a 9-item task plan for building a completely unrelated project. Agent picks up phantom tasks from system prompt context after completing the actual task. Happened twice, indicating a systemic issue with task completion detection.

signals.topic: OpenHands kills its own process on port 8000, crashing the entire service during web app deployment
signals.summary: When launching a local web app, OpenHands checks for available ports and frees port 8000 by killing the process using it — but that process is OpenHands itself, causing the entire service to crash.
signals.review_reason: OpenHands self-terminates its own main process during web app deployment due to a port conflict detection bug. This is a complete service crash — users lose their entire session. The bug is in the port allocation logic where OpenHands kills its own process to free a port it was already using.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: OpenHands kills its own process on port 8000 during local web deployment
source_issues.evidence: OpenHands checks for available port and frees port 8000 by terminating the process using it. Problem: port 8000 was being used by OpenHands itself, so OpenHands killed its own main process and crashed the entire service. This is a self-destructive bug in port allocation logic.

signals.topic: SendWebRequestBlock failures causing web request operations to be blocked
signals.summary: The SendWebRequestBlock component raises BlockUnknownError for multiple failure modes (connection timeout, unknown error, too many redirects), preventing agents from fetching web content — a core functionality for autonomous agents that rely on real-time web data.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct issues all originating from the same SendWebRequestBlock component, each with a different failure mode (timeout, unknown error, redirects). This represents a systemic web request reliability problem that blocks core autonomous agent functionality — agents cannot fetch web content, which is essential for research and information-gathering tasks. The errors are user-visible through the linear[bot] reporting system, confirming they are real failures affecting production use.

source_issues.evidence: SendWebRequestBlock raises BlockUnknownError with connection timeout to web.archive.org, blocking the agent from fetching archived web content.

signals.topic: Marketplace agents download with incorrect/outdated titles instead of published marketplace titles
signals.summary: When downloading an agent from the marketplace, users receive the original title set by the creator in their library rather than the title published in the marketplace, and agent images are not downloaded. This causes confusion and breaks the expected behavior that the agent appears identically in the library as it does in the marketplace.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues affecting the marketplace feature: (1) agents download with incorrect titles and missing images, breaking expected user experience of marketplace-to-library parity, and (2) the StoreAgent database relation is missing, causing a RawQueryError that makes the marketplace store agents entirely inaccessible. Together these represent a degraded marketplace experience that affects users trying to discover and download agents. Count=2 with single-repository scope results in P2 priority.

source_issues.title: Marketplace data should be downloaded with Agent
source_issues.evidence: When downloading an agent from the marketplace, the title is the old creator-set title instead of the marketplace-published title, and agent images are not downloaded. The expected behavior is that the agent appears in the library exactly as it does in the marketplace. Confirmed by maintainer (Torantulino) as an active issue.

source_issues.title: DatabaseError: Failed to fetch store agents
source_issues.evidence: RawQueryError: relation 'StoreAgent' does not exist in the database, causing the store agents feature to fail entirely with a database error.

signals.topic: 多 ClawX 进程并发时 Gateway RPC 阻塞，导致飞书和本地客户端同时断连且对话历史丢失
signals.summary: 当多个 ClawX 进程同时向 Gateway 发送 RPC 请求时，Gateway RPC 队列阻塞，chat.history 超时（30秒），导致飞书消息和本地对话同时丢失，需要重启才能恢复。
aliases: 多进程资源竞争导致对话丢失
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断且对话历史丢失：Gateway RPC 超时导致飞书消息和本地对话同时丢失，是严重的数据完整性破坏。用户提供了详细的根因分析和架构图，证据充分。虽仅 1 条 issue 但影响所有客户端，定 P1。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 5 个 ClawX 进程 → Gateway 资源竞争 → 不停的断连
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供详细的根因分析：5 个 ClawX 进程同时连接 Gateway (端口 127.0.0.1:18789)，RPC 队列处理能力和 WebSocket 连接数有限，导致 chat.history 请求超时 30 秒，飞书消息和 ClawX UI 对话均丢失。影响所有客户端。

signals.topic: 并发 arun() 共享 session_id 时 Session runs 数据静默丢失

source_issues.evidence: 完整可运行复现代码 + 明确竞态窗口描述（acleanup_and_store 中 session 提前加载，LLM 推理期间另一并发请求覆盖数据）。数据丢失无错误警告。

signals.topic: Shell/TUI tool output visibility and UI panel flickering when 'Hide tool details' is enabled
signals.summary: When 'Hide tool details' is enabled, user-initiated shell commands (via !), AI-invoked tool calls, and TUI panels (Toggle Review, Toggle File Tree) all experience visibility issues: shell output disappears after execution, tool calls flicker before vanishing, and panels flicker/reset to loading state. Root cause is the shouldHide logic in ToolPart only checking for completed status, leaving running/pending states visible.
aliases: Hide tool details causes tool flicker
signals.review_reason: Count=5 (5 distinct issues, same root cause in shouldHide/UI state logic), P0 because it affects core interaction blocking visibility of both user-initiated shell commands and AI tool outputs. Multiple users report content disappearing/flickering across shell, tool calls, and panels.

source_issues.title: Shell mode (`!`) output hidden when 'Hide tool details' is enabled; AI-invoked tools flicker before hiding
source_issues.evidence: Shell command output appears briefly then disappears. AI-invoked tools flash on screen while running then vanish. shouldHide only checks status === 'completed', leaving running/pending visible.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Toggle Review and Toggle File Tree panels flicker/reset after loading
source_issues.evidence: Toggle Review and Toggle File Tree panels briefly load correctly then reset/flicker/return to empty state. Persists after restart.

source_issues.title: Background agents cannot be force-interrupted/stopped via ESC
source_issues.evidence: Background agents cannot be interrupted via ESC after being backgrounded. User must force-kill. Affected multiple past versions.

source_issues.title: Plan mode does not prevent write operations via Bash tool
source_issues.evidence: Agent in plan mode (read-only) successfully ran git commit --amend via Bash tool. Write operations not blocked despite plan mode designation.

source_issues.title: Edit tool applies session project's formatter instead of target file's formatter for cross-project edits
source_issues.evidence: Editing a file in project-B applies Biome formatter from session project-A instead of Prettier from project-B. Results in 72 insertions/77 deletions for a 3-line change.

signals.topic: Diff pipeline and session summarize cause severe UI lag on desktop — still runs despite snapshot:false config
signals.summary: The diff pipeline (VCS diff and SessionSummary) causes severe UI jank on the desktop app due to full-context unified patches, synchronous main-thread parsing, and whole-array reconcile on every SSE event. Additionally, even with snapshot:false, SessionSummary.summarize() still runs its full pipeline — loading all messages from DB, writing empty summaries, publishing empty SSE events — causing redundant DB I/O and UI re-renders.
aliases: SessionSummary summarize perf despite snapshot false
signals.review_reason: Two related issues: (1) Diff pipeline causes actual UI freezes/lag on desktop, blocking work; (2) snapshot:false config is violated — users who explicitly disabled it for performance reasons still pay full overhead. Both have clear root cause analysis and measurable impact.

source_issues.title: perf: diff pipeline causes severe UI lag on desktop — full-context patches + synchronous parsing on main thread
source_issues.evidence: Disabling diff systems eliminates lag entirely, confirming diff as root cause. Synchronous main-thread parseDiffFromFile in SessionReview.items() causes UI freeze. Full-context patches (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER context) amplify payload size. 7 createMemo per file + getBoundingClientRect per scroll frame causes sustained frame drops.

source_issues.title: bug: `snapshot: false` config does not prevent summarize() from running — still causes DB writes and SSE events
source_issues.evidence: Users who set snapshot:false expecting reduced overhead still get: DB reads (loading all messages), DB writes (empty summaries), bus event publishing (empty diff events), frontend reconcile and re-renders — all on every assistant message, twice per message.

signals.topic: OpenCode Desktop prompt marked complete but nothing executes (silent failure — background server crash/disconnect)
signals.summary: In OpenCode Desktop, after posting prompts the system immediately returns 'completed' without actually executing anything. The UI appears normal but the background server has crashed or lost connection to the UI. This blocks the entire main workflow.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow completely blocked with no error indication. User has no visibility into failure. Worked before same version. Confirmed by author as 'silent failure' — critical UX failure pattern.

source_issues.title: OpenCode 1.4.6 'silent failure' behavior
source_issues.evidence: After posting prompts, OpenCode Desktop returns 'completed' instantly but does nothing. Background server has crashed or lost connection to UI. Worked fine before. No error shown to user — completely silent failure.

signals.topic: Web UI crashes when browsing nested directories (3+ levels deep) in project picker
signals.summary: The web UI crashes when trying to open or search for a folder more than 2-3 levels deep in the project picker. The directory picker creates full server instances (with file watchers, LSP, snapshots) for each intermediate directory, exhausting inotify limits and memory on Linux, crashing the process.
signals.review_reason: Critical workflow block: users cannot open their projects in web UI if they have standard nested directory structures (e.g. ~/projects/org/repo). Process crash, not recoverable without fix. Root cause clearly identified (over-initialization per directory level).

source_issues.title: Web UI crashes when browsing folders in the project picker
source_issues.evidence: Browsing to ~/projects/org/repo crashes the opencode process. Directory picker boots full server instance per intermediate directory (file watchers, LSP, snapshots). 4 levels = 4+ concurrent instances. Exhausts inotify watch limits on Linux and memory. No workaround.

signals.topic: Web interface 'Open Project' dialog exposes user's entire home directory to all path access
signals.summary: When using 'opencode web' and selecting 'Open Project', the file picker shows the entire home directory instead of scoped project paths. Users cannot restrict the dialog to a specific project directory, creating a permission over-exposure issue in multi-user or shared environments.
signals.review_reason: Security-relevant permission over-exposure: the 'open project' dialog has no path restriction mechanism, exposing the full home directory. While a single reporter, this is a clear architectural gap in the web interface's permission model.

source_issues.title: When i am in the web interface and select open project it shows content of my home folder
source_issues.evidence: User cannot restrict the 'open project' dialog to show only specific paths. Home folder contents are exposed. User explicitly asking how to restrict access indicates no built-in permission scoping mechanism.

signals.topic: ToParam() serialization drops required fields, causing 400 errors in agentic loops
signals.summary: Beta Managed Agents event helpers (BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage) and ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() omit required fields (Type/error_code) due to missing initialization or omitzero behavior, resulting in 400 Bad Request when calling the API or during multi-turn agentic loops.
aliases: BetaManagedAgents event helper missing Type field

Both are in beta API paths, both break the API call or agentic loop, both have workarounds but no fix. Count=2 meets P1 threshold without requiring P0. Note: P1 not P0 because both have documented workarounds and neither has comments suggesting widespread user impact yet.

source_issues.title: BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage helper omits required Type field
source_issues.evidence: Calling BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage() results in 400 Bad Request with 'events[0].type: Field required'. The helper only sets Content, not Type. Has workaround (construct struct directly).

source_issues.title: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops required error_code field via omitzero
source_issues.evidence: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops error_code via omitzero tag when ErrorCode resolves to empty string, causing 400 'Field required' on next agentic-loop iteration. Has workaround (raw JSON passthrough). Related to #242 same bug in WebSearchToolResultBlock.

signals.topic: Official documentation examples use types that don't exist in the SDK, blocking beta feature usage

SDK types missing for beta managed agents

P1 not P0 because single-issue count without further corroboration.

signals.topic: Java structured output schema: all fields marked required, ignoring @Nullable / Optional nullability — forces LLM to hallucinate values
signals.summary: The Java SDK's internal schema generator for StructuredOutput treats ALL Java class fields as mandatory (adding them to JSON Schema `required` array), ignoring @Nullable annotations and Optional<T> types. This causes LLMs to hallucinate placeholder values (string "null", empty strings, dashes) to satisfy schema constraints, directly degrading structured output quality.
signals.review_reason: 用户报告了明确的功能缺陷：结构化输出功能的 schema 生成器完全忽略 Java 的 nullability 标记，将所有字段强制设为 required。这直接导致 LLM 生成无意义的占位值（字符串'null'、空字符串、破折号），属于关键功能（结构化输出）质量严重下降，是用户主流程中反复遇到且目前无法绕过的阻断性问题。用户提供了可复现的代码示例和 schema 对比，证据充分。

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports that @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and Optional<T> are all ignored — every field lands in the required array, causing LLM to hallucinate 'null' strings and empty strings to satisfy constraints. 3 comments from other users confirming the same pattern.

signals.topic: beta.skills.list hard-capped at 100 items — silent data loss and false duplicate errors block skill provisioning workflows

signals.review_reason: Blocks skill enumeration workflows for accounts with >100 skills — causes silent data loss (invisible skills), false 400 duplicate errors on create, and inability to delete orphaned skills. The workaround is fragile and wastes API calls. A hard cap that silently truncates results with no cursor is a clear user-impacting failure.

source_issues.title: beta.skills.list hard-capped at 100 items with broken pagination (has_more always false, no cursor)
source_issues.evidence: Account with ~120 skills: skills.list() returns exactly 100 items regardless of limit param (10/50/100/500/1000 all yield 100). has_more=false, no next_page/after_id cursor. False 'duplicate display_title' 400 errors at create time for skills in the invisible tail. Cannot look up skill_id to delete invisible skills.

signals.review_reason: Accumulating storage cost with no safe cleanup path. Users cannot distinguish referenced files from orphans, making any deletion attempt unsafe. This is a direct cost and data-integrity issue for any multi-skill account.

source_issues.title: Cannot GC orphan Files API files — skill→file linkage not exposed on skills.versions.retrieve
source_issues.evidence: ~1100 files on a single account, zero identifiable as orphan vs. in-use. beta.skills.versions.retrieve returns no files field. beta.files.list has no skill_id filter or scope filter. Cannot safely delete without breaking live skills. Each provisioning cycle adds more orphan files.

Streamable HTTP MCP not supported in Managed Agents

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE endpoint April 1 2026. Any Managed Agents session with Apify MCP server fails at init with 'MCP server apify initialize failed: SSE data line is not valid JSON'. Server returns 405 for SSE. No client-side workaround available. Agent falls back to other tools and never uses Apify.

signals.topic: Managed Agents events.stream() silently drops all events — streaming API entirely broken in SDK 0.93.0

All managed agents event types (session.status_*, agent.message, agent.tool_use, etc.) are silently dropped. events.list() polling still works; only streaming is broken.

All managed agents events (session.status_running, agent.message, agent.tool_use, etc.) have no match and are silently dropped. Minimal repro: fake SSE with 3 managed agents events yields 0 received events. Affects every consumer of events.stream(). Closed as bug, reopened or still active.

signals.topic: Skills API returns immediate HTTP 500 when skills are enabled — blocks all skills-enabled requests with no error details
signals.summary: When skills are enabled on requests, the API returns an immediate HTTP 500 with no useful error payload. Disabling skills and using the general Messages API succeeds. All skills-enabled requests fail.
signals.review_reason: All skills-enabled requests fail with immediate HTTP 500 — this is a complete outage of the skills feature. Users must disable skills entirely to use the API, losing dynamic context and tool pipeline functionality.

source_issues.title: Bug: Skills API returns immediate 500s when skills are enabled (base API works)
source_issues.evidence: Same request without skills: succeeds. With skills enabled: immediate HTTP 500 with no structured error body. 500 returned instantly (no processing latency), suggesting server-side crash not model execution failure. Forces fallback to reduced functionality mode.

signals.topic: SDK silently drops ping SSE events, preventing stream liveness detection and causing indefinite hangs with no recovery
signals.summary: The SDK drops all ping events (continue; statement) and does not expose them in RawMessageStreamEvent. This makes it impossible for downstream consumers to detect stream liveness, distinguish 'stalled' from 'slow', or implement a ping-aware watchdog. Combined with no SDK-level idle timeout, streams that stall mid-stream (network issues, server stalls) hang indefinitely with no error, no timeout, and no recovery. Claude Code is affected by this at scale (#46987 with 40+ reports).
signals.review_reason: This is a multi-incident pattern confirmed across 2 issues (count=2). #867 documents a real production Claude Code hang with 15+ minutes of lost work, 0% CPU (process stuck, not processing). #749 is explicitly the root cause: the SDK drops ping events, making liveness detection impossible. #998 further confirms this is the root cause of Claude Code #46987 (40+ user reports). This is a P0: high frequency impact (affects Claude Code at scale), main workflow blocking (process hangs forever with no recovery), and sample links are available.

source_issues.title: include ping and error in RawMessageStreamEvent
source_issues.evidence: Maintainer RobertCraigie acknowledged: 'We don't include ping or error because the SDK will never yield those events.' Manucorporat responded: 'I think it's still valuable to receive the ping events in the async iterator, it's useful for detecting if the connection is still alive.' Issue open 11 months with no action.

source_issues.title: bug/proposal: infinitely hanging clients breaking bigger/complex sessions. Proposal: add Streaming Idle Timeout to Prevent Indefinite Hangs
source_issues.evidence: Documented real production incident: Claude Code session at 0% CPU sleeping indefinitely with no error. No existing timeout mechanism detects stalled streams. Existing timeout options fail because the request already started receiving data. 15+ minutes of lost productivity. Explicitly describes 'streamed with stop_reason: null, then no more events arrived — the stream didn't close, didn't error, didn't timeout — it simply stopped sending data.'

signals.topic: Streaming parser crashes with unhandled SyntaxError on invalid JSON escape sequences from model output
signals.summary: When Claude outputs strings containing regex-like escape sequences (e.g. \d, \p, \s) inside JSON, the streaming parser's JSON.parse throws an unhandled SyntaxError that crashes the entire Node.js process. No recovery path exists.
aliases: JSON.parse crash on invalid escape sequences
signals.review_reason: This is a real application crash (unhandled rejection) that blocks the main message streaming workflow. It occurs during a core API interaction and has a reproducible test case. While count=1, the impact is severe (process termination) and the fix is well-scoped, warranting P1.

source_issues.title: bug(streaming): JSON.parse crashes on invalid escape sequences in model output
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows unhandled SyntaxError crashes the Node.js process. Triggered by models producing JSON with regex patterns, Windows paths, or LaTeX. No recovery strategy exists — the application terminates.

signals.topic: O(N²) string concatenation performance in MessageStream text accumulation causes severe degradation for long responses
signals.summary: MessageStream accumulates streamed text via `accumulated += chunk`, which is O(N²) in JavaScript due to string immutability. Each concatenation copies the entire accumulated string, causing severe performance degradation and memory issues for long responses (code generation, structured JSON output).
signals.review_reason: Performance degradation on core streaming path is a significant user pain point. The O(N²) behavior is mathematically proven and directly impacts users doing code generation or long JSON output. Although count=1, the issue is clearly documented with a benchmark and has a known fix (array-based accumulation).

source_issues.title: perf(MessageStream): O(N²) complexity in text accumulation during structured output streaming
source_issues.evidence: Explicit benchmark showing O(N²) behavior. At 128K tokens, elapsed time grows quadratically with token count. Users performing code generation or structured JSON output experience noticeable slowness and memory overhead.

signals.topic: toolRunner fails to propagate container.id across iterations, and setMessagesParams workaround causes infinite tool-call loop
signals.summary: Two compounding bugs when using client.beta.messages.toolRunner with code_execution_20260120 and client-side betaTool: (1) container.id is silently dropped between iterations, causing API invalid_request_error; (2) the only available workaround (setMessagesParams) corrupts message history and triggers an infinite duplicate tool-call loop. No working path exists for this use case.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow block — the user explicitly states there is NO working path to use client-side betaTools with code execution in toolRunner. Both bugs compound to eliminate all possible workarounds. This is a P0-level blocking issue.

source_issues.title: Bug: `toolRunner` does not propagate `container.id` across iterations, and `setMessagesParams` causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: Two compounding bugs with zero workaround. Bug 1: API returns 'container_id is required' error on subsequent iterations. Bug 2: setMessagesParams workaround causes infinite loop with duplicate tool calls and no termination. Explicitly states 'There is currently no working path to use client-side betaTools alongside code_execution_20260120 in a streaming toolRunner loop.'

signals.topic: docx and pptx Agent Skills fail silently during streaming — stream ends without Message or error
signals.summary: When using container.skills with docx or pptx skills, the stream terminates without producing a Message and without throwing any error. Users receive no feedback that the skill failed. The pdf and xlsx skills work correctly, making this a selective regression in docx/pptx functionality.
signals.review_reason: Key documented functionality (docx and pptx skills) is silently broken with zero user feedback. This is not a blocking issue per se, but the silent failure means users cannot use document processing skills at all — they get no output, no error, and no indication of what went wrong.

source_issues.title: Agent Skills: docx and pptx skills fail silently with streaming
source_issues.evidence: Stream ends without producing a Message with role=assistant. No error is thrown. 6 comments indicate ongoing discussion. docx and pptx are documented skills but fail silently while pdf and xlsx work — a clear regression in specific skill functionality.

signals.topic: query() with mcp_servers closes stdin prematurely, blocking MCP handshake
signals.summary: When using query() with a string prompt and mcp_servers, the SDK unconditionally closes stdin after writing the user message, causing CLIConnectionError when the CLI later tries to register the MCP server via stdin. Affects MCP tool usage in query() mode.
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks the main use case of using custom MCP servers with the query() API — the MCP handshake fails before any model call, making mcp_servers entirely unusable in query() mode. Users get CLIConnectionError immediately. Explicitly linked to two previously closed issues (#295, #730) showing this is a recurring, known pattern.

source_issues.title: query() + mcp_servers: string-prompt branch closes stdin before MCP handshake, not fixed by #731
source_issues.evidence: CLIConnectionError: ProcessTransport is not ready for writing during MCP server handshake, before any model invocation. Reproduces same class of symptom as closed issues #295 and #730. PR #731 removed timeout-based stdin close but client.py still calls transport.end_input() unconditionally.

source_issues.title: mcp_servers + query() fails: 'ProcessTransport is not ready for writing' (closed, unfixed)
source_issues.evidence: Related closed issue showing same symptom: mcp_servers + query() fails with ProcessTransport not ready for writing.

signals.topic: SDK lacks feature parity with Claude Code CLI: disable-model-invocation behavior mismatch and slash commands unsupported
