signals.review_reason: SDK users cannot use slash commands at all, and disable-model-invocation behaves differently from CLI — these are direct feature gaps that prevent SDK parity with the CLI experience. Users migrating workflows from CLI to SDK hit immediate blockers.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent behavior of disable-model-invocation: true between Claude Code and Agent SDK
source_issues.evidence: disable-model-invocation: true in custom Skills slash command works in Claude Code but fails or produces no result when triggered via Agent SDK. SDK enforces the flag strictly, preventing the agent from triggering the skill, whereas Claude Code has an alternative execution path.

source_issues.title: slash commands
source_issues.evidence: User asking how to use slash commands through the SDK. When attempting through SDK or directly to CLI, it produces no output. Question about auto-detecting .claude/commands presence or a flag to pass a commands directory.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group cancel scope leak causes 100% CPU loop on query() completion
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport uses an anyio task group anti-pattern that causes cross-task cancel scope exit on every normal query() completion. This cancels the caller's task and pins anyio's _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU loop until the process restarts.
signals.review_reason: This causes a 100% CPU spin loop that effectively hangs the process after every normal query() completion. It is a direct crash/hang equivalent triggered by normal SDK usage. The issue explicitly identifies this as the same bug pattern fixed in PR #746 for query.py, indicating a known, recurring architectural flaw.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Every normal completion of async for message in query(...) triggers a cross-task cancel scope exit on async-generator finalization, which cancels the caller's task from an unrelated context and pins anyio's _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU loop until the process restarts. Same underlying bug pattern as #454 and #776.

signals.topic: SDK crashes fatally on HTTP 429 rate limit, destroying long-running agent sessions
signals.summary: Agent SDK crashes fatally when the API returns a 429 rate limit error, even though this is transient and recoverable. Multi-turn autonomous sessions accumulating 10+ minutes of work are destroyed by a single rate limit hit. On a 30k tokens/minute rate limit, any agent reading files larger than ~10KB reliably crashes within 10-15 minutes.
signals.review_reason: This destroys user work — long-running autonomous agent sessions that accumulate minutes of state are terminated by a single transient HTTP error that should be recoverable. The description provides specific, quantifiable impact: 10-15 minute crash window on typical workloads. This is a primary flow failure with clear cost/time loss for the user.

source_issues.title: Agent SDK should handle 429 rate limits gracefully instead of crashing
source_issues.evidence: SDK crashes fatally on 429. Multi-turn autonomous sessions (10+ min of work) destroyed by a single rate limit. On 30k tokens/min rate limit, any agent reading files >10KB reliably crashes within 10-15 min. User loses all accumulated work. Transient, recoverable HTTP errors should be retried with Retry-After delay.

signals.topic: MCP tool result handler silently drops search_result content blocks, breaking RAG citations
signals.summary: Custom tools defined with @tool that return search_result content blocks have those blocks silently discarded before reaching Claude. The MCP tool result handler only recognizes text and image content block types, so search_result falls through and is silently dropped, preventing use of native citations with custom RAG pipelines.
signals.review_reason: search_result content blocks are silently dropped with no error or warning, breaking a core RAG/citation use case. Users have no indication that their tool's output was discarded — citations simply fail to appear. This is a silent data loss in a critical data pipeline path.

source_issues.title: search_result content blocks silently dropped by MCP tool result handler
source_issues.evidence: MCP tool result handler in claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py only recognizes text and image content block types. search_result blocks fall through both checks and are silently discarded. Users building custom RAG tools expecting native citation support have the feature silently fail with no error.

signals.topic: PostToolUse callback hooks: return value silently discarded, breaking MCP tool output updates and transcript integrity
signals.summary: When all PostToolUse hooks are JavaScript callbacks (no shell/prompt/agent/function hooks), the SDK's callback-only fast path in hook executor Xh discards the hook return value entirely. updatedMCPToolOutput is never yielded, so live API calls don't see replacements and session transcript JSONL retains original tool responses instead of hook-modified ones. Only works when at least one non-callback hook is registered.
aliases: updatedMCPToolOutput silently ignored in callback-only hook path
signals.review_reason: This is a silent data-integrity bug with clear user impact: callback-only hook users cannot get updatedMCPToolOutput propagated to API calls or persisted to transcripts. The feature appears to work (no errors thrown) but data is silently wrong. Root cause traced to specific SDK source path (Xh fast path). Confirmed P0 due to complete functional failure for the affected code path.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse callback hooks: return value (updatedMCPToolOutput) silently discarded, never persisted to transcript
source_issues.evidence: Root cause confirmed in SDK source (Xh function): callback-only fast path calls hook but discards return value then exits without yielding. updatedMCPToolOutput is silently dropped. Transcript JSONL keeps original tool response. Workaround: TOON-encoding at persist time.

signals.topic: stdin closed after first result causing 'Stream closed' cascade — MCP tools and PostToolUse callbacks fail after Monitor task-notification continuations
signals.summary: When using async-iterable prompts with bidirectional controls (hooks, SDK MCP, canUseTool, elicitation), Query.streamInput calls transport.endInput() after the first result, closing CLI stdin. When a Monitor task-notification queues a continuation after that result, C_8.sendRequest() throws 'Stream closed' for all subsequent MCP tool calls and hook callbacks. Observed in real SDK sessions with exact timestamps showing MCP screenshot call returning 'Error: Stream closed'.
aliases: Stream closed error after Monitor task-notification
stdin EOF cascades to MCP tool failures
transport.endInput race with queued task continuations
signals.review_reason: This is a production-blocking bug for async-iterable prompt users with MCP tools or hooks: after the first result, all MCP tool calls and PostToolUse callbacks fail with 'Stream closed'. Real session timestamps confirm the cascade. The bug occurs in a specific but common workflow (async prompts + hooks/MCP), making it a high-severity main-flow blocker for affected users.

source_issues.title: SDK closes stdin after first result while CLI can continue from Monitor task-notification, causing Stream closed cascade
source_issues.evidence: Real timeline: Monitor calls return at 04:51:53, queued task-notification injected at 04:52:12, mcp__browser__screenshot at 04:52:17 returns 'Error: Stream closed'. Every later MCP tool and PostToolUse callback fails. Minimal fake-process repro provided showing SDK closes stdin after first result regardless of session continuation. Root cause: streamInput calls transport.endInput() via waitForFirstResult then ProcessTransport.endInput() triggers processStdin.end(), flipping inputClosed=true in C_8.

signals.topic: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' with no structured_output for non-trivial/nested JSON schemas — feature appears broken for common use cases
signals.summary: Using outputFormat with nested or complex JSON schemas (objects with nested properties, arrays of objects, enums, additionalProperties constraints) returns subtype 'success' but structured_output is undefined. The model correctly generates JSON in result text but the SDK does not extract or validate it. Users cannot distinguish 'schema unsupported' from 'success with no structured data'.
aliases: outputFormat broken for complex JSON schemas
signals.review_reason: outputFormat is a key SDK feature for getting type-safe structured data. When it silently returns undefined for non-trivial schemas while claiming success, users lose the primary benefit of the feature. They cannot programmatically distinguish 'schema too complex' from 'success with no data', forcing manual parsing of result text. This breaks a core promised capability for common schema shapes.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent — should return error_max_structured_output_retries
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows simple 2-field schema works but any nested structure (3 levels, enums, arrays of objects, $ref) fails silently. Raw Messages API handles these schemas correctly, proving it's an SDK extraction/validation issue. Model generates correct JSON in result text but SDK doesn't extract it. 4 comments indicate others hit the same issue.

signals.topic: instance.interrupt() is flaky — session does not reliably pause, interrupt() completion not logged in some cases
signals.summary: Manual user pause via instance.interrupt() works in most sessions but intermittently fails to reach the expected completion path. Failed logs show multiple repeated interrupt() calls over several minutes (09:15-09:19) without an 'interrupt() completed' log, while successful logs show immediate completion within the same call. The intermittent nature makes it unreliable for production use.
signals.review_reason: interrupt() is a critical control mechanism for users who need to safely pause or abort agent sessions in production. Intermittent failure (sometimes works, sometimes hangs for minutes) creates unpredictable UX and potential resource leaks. Even without exact root cause, the evidence of repeated failed interrupt() calls over 4 minutes is a clear user-impacting reliability problem.

source_issues.title: manual user pause is flaky
source_issues.evidence: Failed log shows repeated interrupt() calls over 4+ minutes (09:15 to 09:19) without reaching completion. Successful log shows immediate completion on same-day session. Exact same code path produces both outcomes, indicating race condition or timing dependency.

signals.topic: options.env does not override values in ~/.claude/settings.json — breaks programmatic API key and base URL control
signals.summary: Environment variables passed via options.env do not take effect when the same variable is defined in ~/.claude/settings.json. The value from settings.json is used instead, contradicting documented behavior that 'programmatic options always override filesystem settings'. Developers using Claude Code interactively (which writes config to settings.json) cannot programmatically control which API key or base URL the SDK uses, forcing them to manually remove settings.json entries to use different credentials in SDK apps.
aliases: settings.json env takes precedence over options.env
signals.review_reason: This bug breaks a fundamental expectation (programmatic options override config files) and has concrete impact: developers cannot use different API keys for SDK vs CLI, cannot use custom base URLs programmatically, and must disrupt their interactive Claude Code setup as a workaround. While count=1, the user impact is significant and well-documented.

source_issues.title: Programmatic options.env does not override env values in ~/.claude/settings.json
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps: set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in settings.json to sk-key-A, pass sk-key-B in options.env — SDK uses sk-key-A. Workaround requires manually removing env field from settings.json, disrupting interactive Claude Code setup. Affects multi-tenant apps, custom base URLs, and dual-key scenarios.

signals.topic: Sensitive-file restore crashes when CLAUDE.md or other sensitive paths are git-tracked symlinks
signals.summary: The action crashes with ENOENT symlink error during the 'Restoring sensitive files from origin/master' step when any sensitive path (CLAUDE.md, .claude, .mcp.json, etc.) is a git-tracked symlink. Introduced in v1.0.89. No workaround exists; action is fully broken for repos using AGENTS.md symlink standard.
aliases: cpSync crashes on symlinked sensitive files
signals.review_reason: This is a complete action failure: every PR run for repos with symlinked CLAUDE.md crashes immediately during the sensitive-file restore step. 100% reproducible, no workaround in latest versions, directly blocks the primary use case (PR review). Count=2 (issues #1220 and #1187), both open/active.

source_issues.title: cpSync fails on symlinked sensitive files
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes 100% reproducibly with 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, symlink' during sensitive-file restore. Also produces cascading tsconfig.json fd leak error. Affects any repo where CLAUDE.md is a symlink (e.g., CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md). No workaround available.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed same root cause: cpSync in restore-config.ts fails because symlink() is called before parent directory exists. Introduced in #1174. Workaround is to pin to v1.0.88. No fix in later versions.

signals.topic: Action crashes on fork PRs due to incorrect git fetch strategy for external branches
signals.summary: When triggered via @claude on a fork PR, the action runs `git fetch origin <branch-name>` which fails because the branch only exists on the fork's remote, not on origin. GitHub exposes fork PR content at refs/pull/<number>/head but the action doesn't use it. External contributor workflow is completely blocked.
aliases: claude-code-action fails to checkout fork PRs
git fetch fork external PR branch
signals.review_reason: Fork PR support is a core workflow for external contributors. The action is completely non-functional for this use case: crashes at git fetch step with no workaround. Affects any repo accepting external contributions. Count=2 (#1218 open, #962 closed as duplicate), both explicitly blocked.

source_issues.title: Fork PRs fail: action fetches branch by name instead of using refs/pull/N/head
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with 'fatal: couldn't find remote ref <branch-name>' when @claude is tagged on a fork PR. Root cause is explicit git fetch that contacts remote with branch name. All attempted workarounds (pre-fetching) failed. Also leaves stale comment in 'working' state.

source_issues.title: claude-code-action fails to checkout fork PRs
source_issues.evidence: Same failure: 'fatal: couldn't find remote ref' when @claude tagged on cross-repository fork PR. GitHub API provides the fork's clone_url but action uses origin instead. Closed as duplicate.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock auth broken in tag mode (issue_comment + @claude) and globally regressed since v1.0.74
signals.summary: Bedrock authentication fails with 'Could not load credentials from any providers' or validateHeaders errors. Affects both tag mode (issue_comment + @claude, SDK's exitError check crashes immediately) and broader usage since v1.0.74 regression. Entire production workflows using AWS Bedrock are blocked.
aliases: Could not load credentials from any providers bedrock
signals.review_reason: Bedrock auth failure is a production-critical regression: entire AWS-backed CI/CD pipelines are non-functional. Count=2 (#1090 P1, #1201 P2 by reporters). Both confirmed with valid credentials, no API calls made, directly blocks the workflow. P0 due to severity despite P1/P2 labels on individual issues.

source_issues.title: Bedrock auth broken since v1.0.74 — Could not load credentials from any providers despite valid OIDC credentials
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed working OIDC credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN all present) but action fails with 'Could not load credentials from any providers'. Zero tokens consumed, no API call made. Regression since v1.0.74. Production workflow blocked.

source_issues.title: Bedrock validateHeaders error in tag mode (issue_comment + @claude), agent mode works fine
source_issues.evidence: validateHeaders requires x-api-key or authorization header but Bedrock uses AWS SigV4. In tag mode, SDK's exitError check crashes immediately on auth error. Agent mode (prompt input) succeeds with identical config. Timeline shows intermittent failures with same action version. v1.0.91 does NOT fix despite separate SigV4 fix.

signals.topic: gh CLI and GitHub MCP inline-comment tools unavailable when PR targets the default branch
signals.summary: When a PR targets the repository's default branch, gh CLI and mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment tools become unavailable despite being explicitly listed in allowedTools. Same workflow works for non-default branches. Code review and inline commenting features are blocked in the default branch PR context.
aliases: gh CLI unavailable default branch PR
MCP inline comment blocked default branch
signals.review_reason: Explicitly blocks key code review features (gh CLI commands, MCP inline comments) in the most common PR context (default branch targets). Tools are present in the environment but action-level logic makes them unavailable. No workaround described. Affects a primary use case.

source_issues.title: gh CLI and GitHub MCP tools unavailable when PR targets default branch
source_issues.evidence: Workflow with gh CLI and MCP inline comment tools in allowedTools: tools unavailable when PR targets default branch, works for non-default branches. Action reports 'Since neither gh CLI nor the MCP inline comment tool is available'. Tools are physically present in runner environment. Consistent and reproducible behavior.

signals.topic: --model flag in claude_args silently ignored in tag mode, user-specified model not applied
signals.summary: The --model flag specified via claude_args is silently ignored when the action runs in tag mode (triggered by @claude mentions). The SDK always initializes with the tag-mode default model (claude-sonnet-4-6) regardless of user configuration. No warning is logged, so users don't know their model selection has been ignored.
aliases: claude_args model flag ignored tag mode
signals.review_reason: User-explicit model configuration is silently overridden without warning. Causes wrong model to run (potentially higher cost or different behavior than intended). The action's own documentation primes users to expect --model in claude_args to work. Count=1 but impact is clear misbehavior that users cannot detect without inspecting SDK init logs.

source_issues.title: claude_args --model silently ignored in tag mode
source_issues.evidence: --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 in claude_args is silently ignored in tag mode. SDK init event shows 'model': 'claude-sonnet-4-6' regardless of user config. Action's own action.yml example shows --model being set via claude_args, priming incorrect expectations. Workaround exists (env var ANTHROPIC_MODEL) but requires knowing the workaround.

signals.topic: Claude Code executes irreversible on-chain token transfers without user confirmation, causing real financial loss
signals.summary: Claude Code blindly executed a raw ERC20 transfer to a smart contract address, permanently losing $99.88 USDC. No confirmation prompt, no small-amount test, no warning about irreversible blockchain operations.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow failure with concrete user impact: real financial loss of $99.88 confirmed on-chain. The issue is NOT a generic security keyword match — it documents a specific, reproducible failure mode where Claude Code executes irreversible blockchain transactions without any confirmation prompt, guardrail, or test-first check. The transaction hash and wallet address provide irrefutable on-chain evidence. The financial loss is irreversible and directly attributable to the tool's behavior, making this a P0 despite being a single issue.

source_issues.title: SAFETY: Claude Code lost user's $99.88 by blindly transferring USDC to a smart contract
source_issues.evidence: Real financial loss of $99.88 USDC confirmed via on-chain transaction hash (0xce9d7593288161cd443beb7c2cb3cb7395916628ce1e091a9391e35acff644af). Claude Code executed irreversible ERC20 transfer to Polymarket CTF Exchange contract without verifying the correct procedure, without user confirmation, and without a small-amount test. The user explicitly said 'deposit' and Claude guessed the mechanism instead of researching.

signals.topic: Session JSONL files silently deleted during app update — auto-memory saves nothing, months of work permanently lost
signals.summary: Claude Code silently deletes session JSONL files (60,702 messages across 160 sessions), leaving sessions-index.json orphaned pointing to missing files. Auto-memory captures zero meaningful project context, leaving users with no recovery path after data loss.
signals.review_reason: Catastrophic data loss of 160 sessions (60,702 messages) with forensic evidence confirms silent deletion by Claude Code during auto-update. Auto-memory saved zero meaningful content across months of sessions, leaving users with no recovery path and only user-built external archives as lifelines. Both session file deletion and memory system failure are confirmed in two related issues from the same user. This directly blocks the core value proposition of Claude Code as a persistent collaborator.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Claude Code deletes 160 session JSONL files (60,702 messages) — auto-memory saves nothing about months of work
source_issues.evidence: Forensic evidence: sessions-index.json has 160 entries but 0 JSONL files remain on disk. Auto-memory (37 topic files) contains zero references to lost sessions. Gap from Mar 15 – Apr 14 never indexed, files also gone. User lost months of collaborative work. Only external archive (user-built SQLite) recovered data.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Claude ignores user's MEMORY.md and auto-memory files during debugging — treats external memory as disposable
source_issues.evidence: MCP archive server silently fails to connect with no error surfaced. Claude does not read MEMORY.md at session start or when asked about past projects. External archive tools (26 tools) are available but not queried when user asks about past work. Auto-memory saves trivial entries (CSS rules, npm warnings) but misses active partnerships and architectural decisions. Critical MCP failure is silently swallowed.

signals.topic: Rate limit regression — users hitting token limits at 500k-700k tokens, previously able to run sessions of millions of tokens
signals.summary: Users who previously ran sessions of millions of tokens are now hitting rate limits at 500k-700k tokens. The 5-hour usage window appears to be resetting prematurely or the token budget is significantly reduced. Affects power users doing large tasks. No visibility into how sub-sessions contribute to the budget.
aliases: usage data disappears after session init
signals.review_reason: Two users report a significant rate limit regression where sessions that previously ran millions of tokens are now failing at 500k-700k. Additionally, session usage data disappears after session initialization (20% lost within minutes), compounding the budget visibility problem. This represents both a cost loss for users who were previously able to use higher token volumes and a critical lack of transparency into token consumption. Combined evidence from two sources (both marked bug) on the same day strengthens confidence. P1 due to cost impact and unclear scope.

source_issues.title: After just 500k tokens i get - You've hit your limit · resets 2am, and previous it was just 700k tokens. Before last weekend i could do millions.
source_issues.evidence: User reports hitting 'You've hit your limit' at 500k tokens, and previously at 700k tokens. Prior to a recent change (last weekend), the same user could run sessions of millions of tokens. Rate limit now triggers at roughly 1/10th previous capacity. User explicitly asks how to see sub-session token usage, indicating no visibility into budget consumption.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Session Usage Data Disappears After New Session Initialization
source_issues.evidence: User reports 20% of usage disappeared within less than 10 minutes of a new session starting. Usage data vanishes after session initialization, compounding the token budget visibility problem. Combined with #48781, users have both reduced budgets and no visibility into where tokens are consumed.

signals.topic: Claude Code executes unauthorized rm -rf due to APFS case-insensitive path resolution, destroying entire project directory
signals.summary: Claude wrote a file to a typo path with wrong case (WebstormproJects), then ran rm -rf on that path. On macOS APFS (case-insensitive by default), the path resolved to the real ~/WebstormProjects directory, deleting all projects, uncommitted work, and .env files with API keys. Bypassed Trash. No git remote for recovery.
signals.review_reason: Critical, unambiguous data destruction: Claude executed rm -rf that was never authorized, approved, or even initiated by the user. The path collision occurred due to APFS default case-insensitive behavior combined with Claude's own typo. The user's entire project directory (including uncommitted work and API keys in .env files) was permanently deleted. This violates Claude Code's documented safety guardrails. Count=1 but P0 is warranted because: unrecoverable data loss, critical safety failure, affects all macOS APFS users (default filesystem), and demonstrates a systemic gap between documented safeguards and actual behavior.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude Code executed unauthorized rm -rf due to case-insensitive filesystem path resolution
source_issues.evidence: Claude made a typo in a path (WebstormproJects with capital J), then ran rm -rf on that path. On APFS case-insensitive filesystem, the path resolved to ~/WebstormProjects — the real working directory — which was fully deleted. Claude violated its own documented guardrails (NEVER run destructive git commands unless user explicitly requests; check with user before risky actions; measure twice cut once; do not use destructive actions as shortcuts). Entire project directory with uncommitted work and .env files (API keys) permanently lost. Bypassed Trash.

signals.topic: MCP server environment variables silently stripped/renamed before passing to child processes, breaking authentication for Notion and similar MCP integrations
signals.summary: Since Claude Code 2.1.109, MCP server env vars containing tokens are modified before being passed to child processes. NOTION_TOKEN is renamed to NOTION_API_KEY (the Notion MCP server expects NOTION_TOKEN). OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS tokens are stripped entirely. Every Notion API call returns HTTP 401. Verified via process inspection (ps eww). No warning given to user.
signals.review_reason: MCP authentication is a core integration pathway. Claude Code silently modifies or strips tokens from MCP server environment variables, breaking the official Notion MCP server (and potentially any MCP server relying on token-based env vars). Every Notion API call returns HTTP 401, making the integration completely non-functional with no user-visible error. The user had to perform process-level forensics (ps eww) to diagnose the root cause. Regression since v2.1.109. P1 (not P0) because count=1 and only one MCP server explicitly documented as broken, though the pattern likely affects others.

source_issues.title: MCP env vars: tokens stripped from OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS, NOTION_TOKEN renamed to NOTION_API_KEY (v2.1.109)
source_issues.evidence: Verified via ps eww that MCP child process receives NOTION_API_KEY instead of NOTION_TOKEN, and OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS with token stripped. Direct curl to Notion API with same token returns HTTP 200, confirming token validity. Notion MCP server reads NOTION_TOKEN (not NOTION_API_KEY) and expects full token in OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS. Both env var modifications break all Notion API calls (HTTP 401). No error or warning shown to user. Regression from v2.1.109. Workaround requires wrapper script reading from file at runtime.

signals.topic: Concurrent CLI sessions cause authentication failure due to race condition in OAuth token refresh (rotating refresh tokens)
signals.summary: When 4+ concurrent CLI sessions exist and the OAuth access token expires (~8 hours), all sessions race to refresh. With rotating refresh tokens, only the first succeeds; others fail because the refresh token was already consumed. Result: all sessions except one are simultaneously logged out. No file locking or coordination mechanism exists.
signals.review_reason: Race condition in OAuth token refresh causes all concurrent CLI sessions (except one) to be simultaneously logged out. This is a systemic blocker for power users running multiple terminal sessions, SSH connections, or desktop-bridged sessions. The user is a Claude Max subscriber who explicitly pays for multi-session usage, yet the auth system is fundamentally broken for concurrent sessions. No file-locking mechanism exists to coordinate refresh attempts across shared credentials. The 'has repro' label supports this. P1 (not P0) due to count=1 single repo.

source_issues.title: Multiple concurrent CLI sessions cause auth failure on token refresh (race condition)
source_issues.evidence: User runs 4-7+ concurrent CLI sessions (Claude Max subscriber). After ~8 hours when OAuth access token expires, all sessions race to refresh. With rotating refresh tokens, the first session succeeds and invalidates the token other sessions are trying to use. All other sessions fail with /login prompt simultaneously. Root cause: no file-locking or coordination mechanism for shared ~/.claude/.credentials.json. Also claude setup-token may revoke existing refresh token server-side, causing all sessions to fail after setup.

signals.topic: Telegram zombie bun processes spin at 100% CPU — orphan watchdog fails on macOS/Linux; SIGTERM fails on Windows
signals.summary: The orphan watchdog (added in v0.0.5) checks ppid to detect dead sessions, but the immediate parent is the bun wrapper not Claude Code — so ppid never changes. On Windows, SIGTERM cannot terminate bun processes. Zombie pollers spin at 98-100% CPU indefinitely. On Linux/macOS, multiple zombies accumulate, each consuming a full CPU core.
aliases: telegram zombie bun 100% CPU despite v0.0.5 fix
SIGTERM doesn't terminate bun on Windows
orphan watchdog blind spot on macOS Linux
signals.review_reason: count=3 (distinct reporters, #1396 and #1384 open, #1376 Windows-specific) all confirmed as separate accounts of the same root pattern. 100% CPU consumption per zombie causes hardware heating and resource starvation — clear cost impact and system degradation. P0 warranted.

source_issues.title: telegram: orphan watchdog ineffective — zombie bun processes spin at 100% CPU
source_issues.evidence: Two zombies ran 23h and 4h at ~98% CPU. Root cause: ppid check sees bun wrapper, not Claude Code. Bun does not set stdin.destroyed when unix socket closes. Orphan watchdog loop at 5000ms keeps running but never detects orphan.

source_issues.title: [telegram] server.ts pegs 100% CPU per zombie poller despite 0.0.5 fix (#1349)
source_issues.evidence: Zombie bun server.ts processes at 95-100% CPU each on macOS. 0.0.5 process at 14 min CPU time in 14 min wallclock. SIGTERM ignored — must SIGKILL. Different reporter from #1396, confirms cross-platform pattern.

source_issues.title: telegram: stale poller not killed on Windows — SIGTERM doesn't terminate bun processes
source_issues.evidence: Windows zombie pollers cannot be killed via SIGTERM. 409 Conflict persists after 8 retries (~75s), then server exits. Claude Code shows MCP disconnected. SIGTERM semantics on Windows differ from POSIX.

signals.topic: Telegram inbound messages silently not delivered to Claude Code — poll loop exits permanently on non-409 errors
signals.summary: Telegram bot successfully consumes messages (pending_update_count: 0, getUpdates returns empty), but they never appear as <channel source='telegram'> tags in Claude Code. On Windows specifically, messages are consumed but the channel tag fails to surface. Root cause: the poll loop only retries on 409 Conflict — any other error (timeout, TLS reset, DNS, 5xx) causes permanent loop exit, leaving the bot deaf.
aliases: telegram inbound not bridged to Claude Code
inbound messages consumed but not delivered as channel tag
poll loop exits permanently on transient errors
signals.review_reason: count=3 (Windows #1412, Linux #1379, root cause PR #1378) confirmed as independent reports of the same failure mode. Inbound messages being silently swallowed is the core broken promise of the Telegram channel — primary use case failure. P0 warranted.

source_issues.title: telegram v0.0.5: inbound messages consumed but not delivered as channel tag (Windows, CC 2.1.101)
source_issues.evidence: Windows: bot receives messages (pending_update_count: 0, getUpdates returns []). No <channel source='telegram'> tag appears in any CC session. Outbound reply tool works. Confirmed with curl diagnostics. Reproduces across multiple fresh sessions.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin 0.0.5: inbound messages not bridged to Claude Code (outbound works)
source_issues.evidence: Linux: bot process runs and consumes messages from Telegram API but they never reach Claude Code's input stream. Outbound via reply tool works fine. Only one bot process running, no 409 Conflicts.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): poll loop exits permanently on non-409 errors — root cause of 'inbound stops' reports
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: catch block in poll loop logs 'polling failed' and returns, permanently exiting the loop. Any non-409 error (timeout, TLS reset, DNS, 5xx) causes this. Plugin process stays alive (MCP stdin), so outbound works — but bot is deaf. Fix submitted.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin startup PID-steal kills active channel consumer on multi-session load — bot goes offline silently
signals.summary: The bot.pid stale-poller cleanup block at server.ts startup unconditionally SIGTERMs any PID found in bot.pid. When a non-channel CC session loads the plugin, it kills the one active channel consumer, leaving the bot completely offline for that session until manual restart. Complementary issue #1363 shows dual-load also kills the MCP pipe.
aliases: bot.pid SIGTERM kills active consumer on concurrent session
telegram dual-load kills MCP pipe via bot.pid
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (1426, 1363) both show bot.pid SIGTERM mechanism killing active consumers. Count=2 confirms pattern. Users lose Telegram connectivity with no automatic recovery — key functional degradation.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: startup PID-steal kills the active channel consumer when multiple CC sessions load the plugin
source_issues.evidence: Non-channel session B's server.ts SIGTERMs session A's active channel consumer. Session B logs 'replacing stale poller pid=A' but is not a channel consumer itself. Session A's MCP stays disconnected. Reproducible multi-step scenario provided.

source_issues.title: Telegram 0.0.5: bot.pid SIGTERM kills MCP pipe on dual-load — acquireLock is safer

signals.topic: Telegram plugin MCP server fails to start when launched by Claude Code (v0.0.6) — key skills inaccessible

aliases: telegram MCP fails to start under Claude Code
telegram skills inaccessible after MCP disconnect
signals.review_reason: MCP server failing to start is a main-flow block: users cannot pair Telegram, which is the primary value of the plugin. Clear reproduction steps, confirmed MCP failure vs. working channel process, no workaround.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin MCP fails to start when launched by Claude Code (v0.0.6)
source_issues.evidence: MCP server fails silently when launched by Claude Code. Channel process starts and connects to Telegram (confirmed via ps/lsof), but MCP component fails. /telegram:access shows unknown skill. Pairing is inaccessible.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin subprocess dies silently during idle; CLI doesn't respawn — session permanently degraded
signals.summary: The bun server.ts subprocess exits silently after extended idle (hours). Claude Code continues running and claude mcp list falsely reports the plugin as Connected (it spawns a fresh subprocess on each check). The long-running session is permanently degraded — no inbound Telegram messages reach it and every reply tool call fails — until a full CLI restart.
aliases: telegram MCP subprocess dies silently during idle
CLI doesn't respawn dead MCP subprocess
mcp list falsely reports connected after subprocess death
signals.review_reason: Single confirmed report but with severe user impact: long-running session becomes permanently unusable for Telegram (no inbound, no outbound) with no indication from the CLI that anything is wrong. claude mcp list actively misleads. Manual full restart required. Quality degradation of critical workflow.

source_issues.title: [telegram] Plugin subprocess dies silently during idle; CLI doesn't respawn
source_issues.evidence: Process dies after ~3-5h of idle. pgrep confirms no bun process at all. claude mcp list shows Connected because it spawns a fresh subprocess for each check. No OOM kill in dmesg. CLI does not auto-respawn dead MCP stdio subprocess. User had to implement external cron watchdog to detect and trigger tmux-session restart.

source_issues.title: Tutorial using Haiku 3- needs update

signals.topic: Windows 下 skills update 命令因 Node.js 路径含空格而静默失败
signals.summary: 在 Windows 默认安装路径 (C:\Program Files\nodejs\) 下，process.execPath 包含空格且未加引号，当 shell: true 时 cmd.exe 在第一个空格处截断路径，导致 skills update 静默失败，用户仅看到 '✗ Failed to update' 无任何可操作错误信息。
aliases: skills update silent failure on Windows
signals.review_reason: Windows 默认安装路径含空格是极其常见的用户场景，update 主流程静默失败属于主流程阻断，且无任何可操作错误信息，用户体验严重受损。虽然 count=1，但影响路径明确（任何 Windows 默认安装用户都会遇到），属于非边缘阻断问题，应为 P1。

source_issues.title: [Bug] skills update fails on Windows when Node.js path contains spaces
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 用户在默认路径 C:\Program Files\nodejs\ 下执行 npx skills update，命令静默失败，仅输出 '✗ Failed to update <skill-name>'，无错误详情。根本原因：spawnSync 未对 process.execPath 加引号，cmd.exe 在空格处截断路径为 'C:\Program'，子进程 stdio 被设为 inherit/pipe/pipe 导致错误被吞没。

signals.topic: document-skills 与 example-skills 插件加载完全相同的 17 个技能，造成上下文 token 浪费和路由歧义

context waste from duplicate skill loading

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills load identical 17 skills — duplicate context waste

source_issues.title: Symbol not found: _OBJC_CLASS_$_MTLResidencySetDescriptor
source_issues.evidence: Installation aborts immediately after download with dyld error: Symbol not found _OBJC_CLASS_$_MTLResidencySetDescriptor expected in Metal.framework. Binary is compiled against a newer Metal SDK than available on target macOS versions, preventing the app from even starting.

deprecated CLI still required for IDE use

source_issues.title: Claude Code CLI Is Still Required for IntelliJ + Goose Workflow

signals.topic: Summon fails to discover user-level skills (~/.agents/skills) on Windows, only detecting project-local skills

aliases: Windows Summon global skills not detected
signals.review_reason: User-level skill discovery is a documented and expected feature. Its failure on Windows means users lose access to their personal skill library, a key productivity feature. Platform-specific regression that breaks a core extensibility feature.

source_issues.title: Summon detects project skills but not user-level skills on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Windows with goose 1.29: load() lists project-local skills but omits all skills in ~/.agents/skills. Explicit load(source: 'test-summon-c') returns 'Source not found' for user-level skills. HOME and USERPROFILE were correctly set. signals.topic: MCP user elicitation broken on Windows: buttons not appearing, session crashes after selection, default value not selected

source_issues.title: User elicitation does not function correctly with custom MCP server
