aliases: Tool calls not registered with reasoning models
tool_call XML treated as thinking content
signals.review_reason: 工具调用是 Continue 的核心差异化能力，推理模型开启思考后 tool_call 标签被误识别为普通内容直接导致文件修改、搜索等核心编码功能完全失效。虽然 count=1，但影响的是用户主要工作流，review_reason 提供强用户影响证据，符合 P1 评级条件。

source_issues.title: Qwen 3.5 and Gemma 4 can't call tools
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用 LM Studio + Qwen 3.5 9B 和 Gemma 4 26B-A4B 时，模型输出的 <tool_call>...</tool_call> 标签未被注册为工具调用，而是被写入 thinking 部分当作普通消息终结，导致 file_glob_search、edit_existing_file 等核心工具完全不执行。日志显示 Generated Tokens: 0，工具链完全中断。

signals.topic: CLI 的 @file 上下文提供器无法发现 .cc 文件（标准 Unix C++ 扩展名），仅 VS Code 插件正常
signals.summary: Continue CLI 的文件发现逻辑疑似存在硬编码扩展名白名单，缺少 .cc（Unix/Linux/Google 代码库常用）等 C++ 扩展名，导致 @file 无法定位这些文件。VS Code 插件使用相同配置却正常工作，证明是 CLI 特有的实现缺陷。
aliases: @file context provider misses .cc files in CLI
CLI file discovery hardcoded extension allowlist
.cc C++ files not found by @file in CLI
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但用户提供了强对比证据（VS Code 插件正常，相同配置下改后缀 .cpp 即可工作），明确指向 CLI 实现缺陷。.cc 是 Google 等大型代码库的标准扩展名，影响特定工作流用户群体。定性为 P2（低频但有明确用户影响）。

source_issues.title: CLI: @file context provider does not find .cc files
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 Linux 环境下使用 Continue CLI，@file 无法定位 .cc 文件，但相同配置下 VS Code 插件正常工作。.cc 是 Unix/Linux/Google 代码库的标准 C++ 扩展名，覆盖面广。工作区包含 .cc 文件时 CLI 完全无法将其加入上下文，而改名为 .cpp 后立即可用，强烈暗示硬编码扩展名白名单缺失 .cc。

signals.topic: code-server 环境下终端命令输出不可用，阻断代码执行主流程
signals.summary: 在 code-server 环境中运行终端命令时，Continue 返回「Terminal output not available. This is only available in local development environments」错误。code-server 开发者因此无法通过 Continue 执行和验证命令，核心编码流程被阻断。code-server 维护者确认问题不在其侧。
aliases: Terminal output not available in code-server
signals.review_reason: 终端命令执行是代码修改流程的关键环节，code-server 用户占比高（云开发环境普遍使用），该 bug 导致命令执行后无法获取输出，LLM 无法据此决策，主流程阻断。code-server 官方已排除其责任，Kilo Code 对比方案证明技术可行性，指向 Continue 实现缺陷。P1 评级。

source_issues.title: Code-Server bug where it says "Terminal output not available" even though it works on Kilo Code
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 Linux code-server 环境中触发终端命令时收到「Terminal output not available」错误，LLM 无法获取命令输出，导致整个编码辅助流程中断。code-server 维护者确认问题在 Continue 侧，Kilo Code 实现了可用的集成方案，证明该功能在 code-server 中可实现但 Continue 未实现。

signals.topic: Inline Edit 模式在小文件上触发意外的 Token limit 错误，编辑功能不可用
signals.summary: 用户在极小文件（50 行）上尝试 Inline Edit 功能时收到「Token limit reached. File/range likely too large for this edit」错误，并发标签页仅有 2 个小文件，但功能仍无法正常工作。用户怀疑是 DeepSeek R1 模型配置导致。
aliases: Inline edit token limit error on small files
edit mode token limit false positive
signals.review_reason: Inline Edit 是 Continue 的核心差异化功能，在小文件上触发误导性的 token limit 错误导致功能不可用。虽然可能是模型配置问题，但错误消息的误导性和功能的反复失败构成用户痛点。定性 P2（低频单例，但有明确用户影响证据）。

source_issues.title: Error streaming edit diffs: Token limit reached. File/range likely too large for this edit
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 50 行小文件上使用 Inline Edit 功能，contextLength 配置为 8192，但收到「Token limit reached. File/range likely too large for this edit」错误。同一模型在 Chat 模式下正常工作，inline edit 却反复失败。

signals.topic: MCP server recursion error when servers have more than 10 tools
signals.summary: Users cannot use MCP servers with more than 10 tools; adapter fails with RuntimeError: maximum recursion depth exceeded, blocking enterprise integrations like ms-365-mcp-server.
aliases: MCP adapter maximum recursion depth exceeded
signals.review_reason: This is a blocking bug that prevents users from using MCP servers with more than 10 tools, directly blocking real-world enterprise Microsoft 365 integration and similar workflows. Downgraded from P0 to P1 because count=1 < 3, despite blocking severity.

source_issues.title: [BUG] MCP servers over 10 tools causes maximum recursion depth exceeded error
source_issues.evidence: Using MCP servers with more than 10 tools triggers RuntimeError: maximum recursion depth exceeded in the MCP adapter, preventing enterprise integrations such as ms-365-mcp-server from functioning.

signals.topic: output_pydantic/response_model regression causes tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
signals.summary: Since v1.9.0, output_pydantic causes non-OpenAI LLMs (vLLM, LiteLLM) to skip tool calls entirely, returning structured JSON directly from the LLM instead — tools never execute.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression since v1.9.0 that breaks tool execution for all non-OpenAI LLM providers, representing a main flow failure. Downgraded from P0 to P1 because count=1 < 3, despite blocking severity.

source_issues.title: [BUG] output_pydantic / response_model leaks into agent tool-calling loop, causing tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: Since v1.9.0, output_pydantic causes non-OpenAI LLMs (vLLM, LiteLLM) to return structured JSON directly and skip tool calls entirely, meaning tools never execute — a confirmed regression for users on self-hosted or alternative LLM providers.

signals.topic: output_pydantic JSON pattern matching produces false positives with GraphQL and similar brace-delimited content
signals.summary: The JSON_PATTERN regex in converter.py misidentifies GraphQL schemas as JSON due to curly brace matching, causing ValidationError failures when output_pydantic is used with tools that return GraphQL content.
signals.review_reason: Bug causes data corruption/failure when output_pydantic is used with tools returning GraphQL schemas or similar brace-delimited content, causing structured output feature to fail with ValidationError.

source_issues.title: [BUG] when using Task(..., output_pydantic=MyModel) some JSON substring identification within the data occurs with possible false positive
source_issues.evidence: JSON_PATTERN regex in converter.py misidentifies GraphQL schemas as JSON due to curly brace matching, causing ValidationError failures when output_pydantic is used with tools that return GraphQL or similar brace-delimited content.

signals.topic: ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail combination causes TypeError, blocking crew execution
signals.summary: When combining ConditionalTask with output_pydantic and guardrail referencing a context task, CrewAI internally calls json.loads() on a Pydantic object instead of its serialized string, causing TypeError and preventing crew execution entirely.
signals.review_reason: Blocking bug when using the common pattern of ConditionalTask with output_pydantic and guardrails referencing context tasks, causing TypeError and preventing crew execution.

source_issues.title: [BUG] TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not <PydanticModel> when combining ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context
source_issues.evidence: When combining ConditionalTask with output_pydantic and guardrail referencing a context task that also uses output_pydantic, CrewAI internally calls json.loads() on a Pydantic object instead of its serialized string, causing TypeError and blocking crew execution entirely.

signals.topic: Skills system loads all data instead of only metadata, causing prompt bloat and degraded agent performance
signals.summary: The skills system loads all skill data into the LLM prompt instead of only metadata, causing significant prompt bloat when agents have multiple skills activated, leading to degraded performance and increased token costs.
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation through prompt bloat when skills are used, as all skill data is loaded instead of just metadata, increasing token costs and degrading agent performance. Lower confidence due to limited detail in the issue description.

source_issues.title: [BUG] skills problem
source_issues.evidence: The skills system loads all skill data into the LLM prompt instead of only metadata, causing significant prompt bloat and degraded agent performance when agents have multiple skills activated.

signals.topic: renderNodeToOutput crash makes CLI completely unusable after file Edit approval
signals.summary: When a user approves a file edit, the CLI crashes with an unhandled RangeError in renderBorder (String.repeat called with -1), causing the terminal to rapidly blink with debug/error messages. The CLI becomes completely unusable and requires force-killing the process. Stack trace shows deep recursion (x63) in renderNodeToOutput.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker. The core edit-approve flow is completely broken — users cannot complete any file modification task. The crash is a hard failure (unhandled exception + unhandled promise rejection) with a clear stack trace and reproducible steps.

source_issues.title: Error renderNodeToOutput makes CLI unusable after a single Edit file approval
source_issues.evidence: RangeError: Invalid count value: -1 at String.repeat (<anonymous>) at renderBorder at handleContainerNode at renderNodeToOutput (x63). Console rapidly blinks between debug messages and CRITICAL unhandled promise rejection. Reproducible: approve a file edit, CLI immediately crashes.

signals.topic: OAuth token not forwarded to SSE GET request, causing MCP server 401 disconnect
signals.summary: When connecting to an OAuth-protected MCP server via Streamable HTTP transport, the OAuth token is used for the initial POST but not forwarded in the SSE GET notification stream request. The server returns 401, tearing down the entire connection. Users cannot use OAuth-protected MCP servers at all.
signals.review_reason: This blocks an entire class of MCP server integrations — OAuth-protected servers cannot be used at all. The failure is deterministic and verified against a working server. Root cause is clear: the SSE GET path doesn't propagate auth headers.

source_issues.title: StreamableHTTPClientTransport: OAuth token not forwarded to SSE GET request, causing 401 and disconnect
source_issues.evidence: Debug output shows 'Found stored OAuth token' then 'MCP ERROR: Streamable HTTP error: Failed to open SSE stream: Unauthorized'. Verified working via curl with token included. OAuth flow completes and stores token, but _startOrAuthSse() GET request omits Authorization header.

signals.topic: deleteCredentials throws when keychain entry missing, cascading into half-auth state
signals.summary: KeychainTokenStorage.deleteCredentials() throws an error when the underlying keychain has no entry for the server. During re-auth/logout flows, clearCredentials iterates accounts and calls deleteCredentials per account — a throw aborts the loop, leaving users in an unrecoverable half-authenticated state with no path forward.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot clear credentials or complete logout/re-auth flows. The error is thrown mid-loop, leaving the user in a half-authenticated state with no programmatic recovery path. This is a clear auth flow blocker.

source_issues.title: deleteCredentials throws when keychain entry doesn't exist, cascading clearCredentials errors
source_issues.evidence: deleteCredentials throws 'Error: No credentials found for <serverName>' when keychainService.deletePassword returns false. This aborts the clearCredentials loop mid-iteration, preventing logout/re-auth. Users end up in unrecoverable half-auth state.

signals.topic: OAuth refresh tokens silently discarded when access token is rotated
signals.summary: When Google's token refresh endpoint returns only a new access_token (no refresh_token), saveCredentials overwrites the stored credential set verbatim, dropping the existing refresh_token to undefined. Next refresh attempt fails, forcing full re-authentication. Users are periodically kicked out despite having valid stored credentials.
signals.review_reason: This causes periodic forced re-authentication breaks for users who should remain logged in. The root cause (missing merge logic in saveCredentials) is well-documented. Marked possible-duplicate, indicating broader impact.

source_issues.title: OAuth refresh tokens discarded on access_token rotation and on stale-credential delete
source_issues.evidence: saveCredentials overwrites with new payload lacking refresh_token when Google returns only access_token. refresh_token stored as undefined. Next refresh fails. Users forced to re-authenticate periodically. Marked possible-duplicate suggesting wider impact.

signals.topic: CLI stuck in 'Invalid plan' loop blocking agent workflow
signals.summary: After using the /plan command, the agent gets stuck in an 'Invalid plan' loop — even after user approves the plan, it fails to exit plan mode and cannot execute any fixes. This blocks the entire agentic planning/execution workflow.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core agent planning/execution workflow. Users cannot get the agent to exit plan mode and execute work after approving a plan. Marked as possible-duplicate, indicating the issue may affect multiple users.

source_issues.title: Stuck in 'Invalid plan' loop
source_issues.evidence: User approves plan but gets 'Error: Invalid plan' and the agent cannot exit plan mode or apply fixes. Full chatlog provided via gist. CLI version 0.38.0, gemini-2.5-flash-lite.

signals.topic: create_model() credential check ignores api_key in config.toml params section
signals.summary: The early credential validation in create_model() only checks environment variables, completely ignoring api_key configured in the params.api_key field of config.toml. All users who configure API credentials via config.toml are blocked from using configured models.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed reports of the same credential bug. Users with valid API keys in config.toml are blocked from using configured models, forcing env var workaround. This is a clear auth/configuration mismatch that prevents the main model creation flow for all users relying on config.toml-based credentials.

source_issues.title: Bug: create_model() early credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
source_issues.evidence: User has valid api_key configured in config.toml [models.providers.litellm.params.api_key] but create_model() raises ModelConfigError: No credentials found for provider 'litellm'. Workaround: must set LITELLM_API_KEY env var instead.

source_issues.title: Bug: create_model() early credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #2724. Confirms same root cause: credential check only looks at env vars, ignores config.toml params.api_key field.

signals.topic: PatchToolCallsMiddleware crashes agent when thinking token overflow produces invalid tool calls
signals.summary: When thinking tokens overflow and get truncated, the resulting invalid tool calls (in AIMessage.invalid_tool_calls without a corresponding ToolMessage) are not handled by PatchToolCallsMiddleware, causing a BadRequestError 400 that blocks the entire agent workflow.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug. When thinking tokens overflow (common with long chain-of-thought models), the agent crashes with a 400 BadRequestError. The root cause is that PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle AIMessage.invalid_tool_calls that lack a corresponding ToolMessage — a clearly reproducible failure path that directly prevents agent task completion.

source_issues.title: PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle msg.invalid_tool_calls without ToolMessage
source_issues.evidence: AIMessage with invalid_tool_calls (caused by thinking token overflow truncation) leads to BadRequestError 400 when agent attempts to use tool_calls, completely blocking the main invoke() workflow. Reproducible with any model where thinking output exceeds limits.

signals.topic: vLLM thinking token output silently lost in streaming — AIMessageChunk content field stays empty
signals.summary: When using vLLM with thinking mode enabled (enable_thinking: True), the thinking token content is not extracted from the response stream. Users observe ~30+ empty AIMessageChunk(content='') chunks before the first non-empty chunk appears, meaning the model's thinking/reasoning output is completely invisible to consumers of the stream.
signals.review_reason: Significant data loss for vLLM thinking mode users. The thinking/reasoning output that is the core value proposition of thinking models is completely invisible during streaming. This is not a main-flow block (the agent eventually responds) but represents critical observability loss for users who rely on seeing thinking traces.

source_issues.title: AIMessageChunk(content='') for thinking tokens missng from vllm instance
source_issues.evidence: Streaming a vLLM instance with enable_thinking=True produces 30+ consecutive AIMessageChunk(content='') chunks with empty content field. The actual thinking output never appears in the stream. Only after all thinking chunks do empty chunks appear with real content (e.g. '2'). Users cannot see model reasoning/thinking output at all.

signals.topic: /offload CLI command fails with non-OpenAI providers due to dict-serialized message format
signals.summary: The /offload command in the CLI serializes messages in a format that non-OpenAI providers (e.g. anthropic) cannot deserialize, causing the offload operation to fail with 'Got unsupported message type' error.
signals.review_reason: The /offload command (a key CLI memory management feature) is broken for all non-OpenAI providers. Users attempting to offload conversation history on Anthropic, Azure, or other providers receive an unsupported message type error, preventing the stated workflow.

source_issues.title: fix(cli): /offload fails with non-OpenAI providers due to dict-serialized messages
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible by: 1) Configure a non-OpenAI provider (e.g. anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6), 2) Start conversation reaching offload threshold, 3) Run /offload → Error: 'Got unsupported message type: {dict representation of message}'. The /offload is a key CLI workflow for memory management.

signals.topic: arxiv-search skill CLI produces zero output despite successful execution (~530 installs)
signals.summary: The arxiv-search example skill's CLI entry point (arxiv_search.py) calls query_arxiv() but discards the return value — main() never prints the results. The script exits 0 with no stdout/stderr regardless of whether papers were found, making the documented skill completely unusable via CLI.
signals.review_reason: Complete functional failure of a documented skill with ~530 installs. The CLI is advertised to return paper titles and abstracts but produces no output at all — a one-line fix in main() would resolve this. Users cannot use the arxiv-search skill as documented via CLI.

source_issues.title: arxiv-search skill: CLI produces no output (main() drops query_arxiv return value)
source_issues.evidence: Skill reports ~530 installs via 'npx skills'. Running 'uv run --with arxiv python libs/cli/examples/skills/arxiv-search/arxiv_search.py "transformer attention" --max-papers 3' exits 0 with zero stdout and zero stderr. Root cause: main() calls query_arxiv() but drops the return value. SKILL.md explicitly documents that it should return title and abstract for each paper.

signals.topic: InMemoryVectorStore silently drops documents when embedding count mismatches
signals.summary: add_documents uses strict=False zip so embedding mismatch silently truncates document list — no error raised, docs simply lost
signals.review_reason: Causes silent data loss in RAG pipelines — users lose documents without any error indication, leading to incomplete retrieval. Critical data integrity issue only discovered when query results are missing.

source_issues.title: `InMemoryVectorStore.add_documents` silently drops documents on embedding count mismatch
source_issues.evidence: add_documents uses strict=False zip; if embedding model returns fewer vectors than documents passed, zip silently truncates to shorter list. Documents are silently lost with no error. When using BrokenEmbeddings returning fewer vectors than docs, 'Sent 3 docs, got 2 ids back' with no error raised.

signals.topic: InMemoryCache.update incorrectly evicts entries when cache is at maxsize
signals.summary: update() on existing key at maxsize forcefully evicts oldest entry instead of in-place update, causing repeated cache misses
signals.review_reason: Causes repeated cache misses and data loss in production — users expecting cached results get none, forcing expensive LLM calls again. The bug specifically affects the common pattern of updating existing cache entries.

source_issues.title: Feature/Bug: Implement missing Language.PERL separators and fix InMemoryCache maxsize update bug
source_issues.evidence: InMemoryCache.update() checks len(cache)==maxsize and forcefully evicts oldest entry instead of performing in-place update. After updating an existing key at maxsize, the previously updated entry is no longer in cache when it should be. Users lose cached results and must re-execute expensive LLM calls.

signals.topic: AzureChatOpenAI profile inference fails, breaking token limit middleware and structured output detection
signals.summary: Profile loading keys off azure_deployment instead of model name; profile stays None, breaking max_input_tokens and structured_output metadata
signals.review_reason: Blocks production features for Azure OpenAI users using standard patterns — token limit middleware fails to calculate limits, structured output capabilities are unknown. Users must manually work around the issue with no clear error message.

source_issues.title: `AzureChatOpenAI` fails to infer profile data from `model`, breaking profile-dependent features
source_issues.evidence: Azure profile-loading logic keys off deployment_name instead of canonical model name. When using init_chat_model('azure_openai:gpt-4o'), profile stays None. Missing max_input_tokens prevents middleware using fractional token limits from working. Missing structured_output metadata breaks logic checking model capabilities.

signals.topic: Mistral integration broken retry logic and unbounded concurrency causing rate limits
signals.summary: Retries occur for non-retryable errors; asyncio.gather ignores max_concurrent_requests limit
signals.review_reason: Causes workflow blocking through rate limit hits and cost loss from unnecessary retries on permanent errors. Users expecting controlled concurrency get unbounded parallel requests that trigger provider throttling.

source_issues.title: Mistral integration does not properly handle retries and concurrency limits
source_issues.evidence: Retry logic applies broadly without filtering retryable errors — retries occur for non-transient errors causing unnecessary cost. Async calls using asyncio.gather do not enforce concurrency limits (max_concurrent_requests=2), leading to uncontrolled parallel requests. This triggers provider-level throttling and degrades performance.

signals.topic: parse_partial_json crashes on raw carriage return and tab characters in LLM output
signals.summary: Parser escapes \n but not \r or \t; some LLMs emit these control chars causing JSONDecodeError
signals.review_reason: Causes main workflow blocking when LLM outputs certain characters — the parsing fails and the chain cannot continue. Users have no workaround when LLMs emit these control characters in structured output.

source_issues.title: `parse_partial_json` fails on raw `\r` and `\t` inside strings
source_issues.evidence: parse_partial_json already escapes raw \n but does not handle \r or \t, which are also control characters that must be escaped in JSON strings per RFC 8259. Some models emit these raw control characters in their output, causing json.JSONDecodeError: Invalid control character. This breaks JSON parsing for affected LLM outputs.

signals.topic: UnboundLocalError in push_message when callbacks is None
signals.summary: Users encounter UnboundLocalError when calling push_message with default callbacks=None, blocking the main message processing flow.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - default callback parameter causes UnboundLocalError, preventing basic message handling from working.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message when callbacks is None or unexpected type
source_issues.evidence: Users encounter UnboundLocalError when calling push_message with default callbacks=None, blocking the main message processing flow.

signals.topic: Missing typing_extensions dependency in langgraph-cli
signals.summary: Clean environments (e.g. GitHub Actions runners) fail to import langgraph_cli due to missing typing_extensions dependency, blocking CLI usage entirely.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - langgraph-cli fails to import on clean installations, completely preventing CLI usage.

source_issues.title: langgraph-cli 0.4.21: Missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
source_issues.evidence: Clean environments (e.g. GitHub Actions runners) fail to import langgraph_cli due to missing typing_extensions dependency, blocking CLI usage entirely.

signals.topic: TAG_NOSTREAM tag fails to suppress node output messages during streaming
signals.summary: Nodes tagged with nostream still emit messages to stream, breaking per-subagent streaming control for frameworks built on LangGraph.
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation - TAG_NOSTREAM is supposed to suppress all streaming but only suppresses LLM tokens, not node output, breaking expected behavior for streaming control.

source_issues.title: TAG_NOSTREAM inconsistency in StreamMessagesHandler: suppresses LLM tokens but not node output messages
source_issues.evidence: Nodes tagged with nostream still emit messages to stream, breaking per-subagent streaming control for frameworks built on LangGraph.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared metadata causing cross-invocation data leakage
signals.summary: Configurable values like thread_id leak into shared base config metadata, causing data from previous invocations to contaminate subsequent calls.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation - thread_id and other configurable values leak between invocations, contaminating agent state across different users/sessions.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: Configurable values like thread_id leak into shared base config metadata, causing data from previous invocations to contaminate subsequent calls.

signals.topic: add_messages format=langchain-openai silently strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
signals.summary: Message IDs become None and custom additional_kwargs are silently dropped after OpenAI format round-trip, breaking ID-based deduplication and losing custom data.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation - silent data loss breaks message deduplication logic and custom metadata (like UI widgets), causing subtle bugs in applications relying on message IDs.

source_issues.title: bug: add_messages(format=langchain-openai) strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
source_issues.evidence: Message IDs become None and custom additional_kwargs are silently dropped after OpenAI format round-trip, breaking ID-based deduplication and losing custom data.

signals.topic: Workflow node cannot access conversation_history data returned by previous nodes
signals.summary: When a workflow node returns conversation_history as an array, subsequent nodes cannot access that data, blocking workflow data pipeline.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：workflow中节点间数据传递失败，用户配置了对话历史节点后下游节点无法获取数据，导致复杂工作流无法正常执行。Issue #35260 明确展示了此问题，影响workflow核心功能。

signals.topic: Plugin database migration fails after volume deletion, causing 500 errors on plugin management APIs
signals.summary: After deleting the docker volume directory, the plugin daemon's install_tasks table does not exist, causing internal server errors on all plugin-related API calls.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：删除volume后plugin daemon的数据库表缺失，导致所有plugin管理API返回500错误，用户无法使用plugin功能，且日志显示明确的PostgreSQL错误 'relation install_tasks does not exist'。

signals.topic: Ollama LLM returns empty response with 'Non-JSON encountered' finish reason
signals.summary: Using Ollama as the model provider results in empty LLM responses and 'Non-JSON encountered' finish reason, even though Ollama returns fine via curl.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Ollama模型无法正常输出，用户完全无法通过Dify使用Ollama。Issue明确说明curl测试正常但Dify报错，用户尝试修改stream_mode_delimiter无效，证明是Dify端解析逻辑问题。

signals.topic: Plugin update enters infinite error loop with 500 errors, requiring manual Docker restart
signals.summary: After updating Amazon Bedrock plugin, it fails and loops with 500 errors indefinitely until the user manually restarts all Docker services.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+体验严重下降：plugin更新失败后陷入无限错误循环，系统进入不可恢复状态，必须手动重启所有Docker服务才能退出循环。用户无法正常使用plugin更新功能。

signals.topic: Sign-in page enters infinite reload loop, preventing user login on source deployments
signals.summary: Accessing /signin causes the page to reload infinitely, making it impossible to enter credentials. Only works if user manually cancels the loop at the right moment.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：用户完全无法登录系统，是最高级别的阻断性问题。Infinite reload loop导致所有新用户无法访问系统，即使手动取消也需要精确时机，严重影响部署后的首次使用体验。

signals.topic: Metadata filter AND operator silently drops conditions on same key — incorrect search results
signals.summary: When using the AND operator in metadata filters with multiple conditions on the same key (e.g., price > 10 AND price < 20), the _process_metadata_filters function silently drops all but the last condition due to dict.update() overwriting existing nested operators. This causes incorrect search filters to be passed to vector databases, leading to wrong or missing search results — a silent data corruption in core search functionality.
signals.review_reason: Core search path silently returns wrong results due to filter logic corruption. No error is raised, user receives incorrect search results without knowing data was lost. This is a main-flow failure (search) with silent corruption — meets user pain point threshold. Count=1 but single-occurrence is acceptable because review_reason provides explicit user-impact evidence (wrong search results from silent filter overwriting).

source_issues.title: Data Loss in `_process_metadata_filters` with `AND` operator
source_issues.evidence: dict.update() in _process_metadata_filters silently overwrites first condition when same key has multiple operators in AND block; output is {'price': {'lt': 20}} instead of {'price': {'gt': 10, 'lt': 20}} — search returns wrong results with no error raised

signals.topic: OpenClaw plugin silently destroys entire openclaw.json config on any JSON parse error
signals.summary: The openclaw-mem0 plugin's readFullConfig() catches all JSON parse errors and returns an empty object, which then causes the plugin to overwrite the entire openclaw.json with only the mem0 plugin entry, destroying all other configuration (models, providers, channels, auth, etc.). This is an irreversible destructive operation triggered by a single corrupt JSON character.
aliases: config file destruction on parse error
plugin destroys all config on JSON error
signals.review_reason: This is a destructive, irreversible data loss event that affects a core configuration file. Any transient JSON corruption (even a trailing comma in any tool's config section) triggers complete destruction of all OpenClaw settings. This is a primary-flow failure — users cannot use the gateway after the event. Count=1 but severity is catastrophic (total config destruction) and review_reason documents explicit user-impact evidence, justifying P0.

source_issues.title: Plugin silently destroys entire OpenClaw config on JSON parse error
source_issues.evidence: Any JSON parse error in openclaw.json causes the plugin to overwrite the entire file with only the mem0 plugin entry, destroying models/providers/channels/auth; user loses all gateway configuration irreversibly

signals.topic: LLM errors silently swallowed and returned as empty memory — no error propagation to caller
signals.summary: The _add_to_vector_store function catches all exceptions during fact-extraction response parsing, including non-JSON LLM outputs, and sets new_retrieved_facts to [] silently. This makes every transient LLM output glitch indistinguishable from 'no new facts to extract', with no error propagation. Downstream integrators (e.g. aldeia-box issue #148) saw this as empty Memory.add results with no indication that the LLM pipeline was actually broken.
aliases: empty facts returned on LLM error
no error propagation from LLM failures
signals.review_reason: Core memory pipeline silently masks all LLM failures by returning empty results with no error signal. This prevents users/integrators from distinguishing between 'nothing new to store' and 'LLM pipeline broken'. Documented downstream impact (aldeia-box#148) where this caused significant debugging time. This is a main-flow silent failure affecting memory storage correctness.

source_issues.title: _add_to_vector_store catches Exception, silently turning LLM errors into empty fact lists
source_issues.evidence: except Exception swallows all errors including KeyError and TypeError from LLM output; new_retrieved_facts set to [] and no error raised; downstream integrators receive empty Memory.add results with no indication the LLM pipeline failed; documented at aldeia-box#148 where config change caused LLM failure with empty results as only symptom

signals.topic: Ollama embedder uses wrong endpoint /v1/embeddings — search and memory operations fail with TypeError
signals.summary: When using Ollama as the embedder provider, mem0 attempts to call the OpenAI-compatible endpoint /v1/embeddings instead of Ollama's required /api/embeddings endpoint. This causes all embedding-dependent operations (search, add, memory operations) to fail with TypeError: fetch failed, rendering the Ollama integration completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Ollama embedder integration is completely non-functional due to wrong API endpoint. All memory search and storage operations fail. This is a key integration breaking — a supported provider (Ollama) cannot be used at all. Single-occurrence but explicit user-impact evidence (complete breakage of search and add operations).

source_issues.title: mem0 plugin fails with TypeError: fetch failed when using Ollama – wrong embeddings endpoint
source_issues.evidence: Ollama endpoint /api/embeddings is never called; plugin always uses /v1/embeddings causing network failure; all memory operations (search, add) fail with TypeError: fetch failed; complete breakage of Ollama embedder integration

signals.topic: anonymousTelemetryId causes infinite OpenClaw gateway startup failure loop — gateway cannot start
signals.summary: The openclaw-mem0 plugin generates and persists an anonymousTelemetryId on first run, but this field is not declared in the plugin's configSchema (additionalProperties: false) or the ALLOWED_KEYS runtime allowlist. This causes the OpenClaw gateway config validation to fail on every restart, creating an infinite startup failure loop that cannot be resolved without manual intervention.
aliases: infinite restart loop due to unknown config key
signals.review_reason: Plugin causes the entire OpenClaw gateway to fail starting on every restart, creating an unresolvable loop without code changes. This is a startup crash — the gateway does not come up at all, blocking all OpenClaw functionality. Single-occurrence but critical severity (complete gateway outage) justifies P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug][OpenClaw] anonymousTelemetryId not declared in configSchema/ALLOWED_KEYS causes infinite startup failure loop
source_issues.evidence: Plugin writes anonymousTelemetryId on registration; on restart the gateway rejects undeclared field; manually removing the field causes the plugin to re-write it on next registration, repeating the failure loop; gateway cannot start at all

signals.topic: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework adapter incompatible with Agent Framework GA, blocking hosted agent deployments to Azure Foundry
signals.summary: The azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework hosting adapter (1.0.0b17) pins its agent-framework-core dependency to <=1.0.0rc3, making it incompatible with the GA 1.0.1 release. Additionally, agent-framework-azure-ai was renamed to agent-framework-foundry in GA. This prevents any project using the GA release from deploying hosted agents to Azure Foundry via `azd up` / `azd deploy`. The adapter is a mandatory dependency for the `from_agent_framework(agent).run()` pattern.
aliases: GA release dependency conflict blocking deployment
signals.review_reason: This is a deployment blocker with direct user impact: users who upgraded to the Agent Framework GA release (1.0.1) cannot install the hosting adapter needed to deploy agents to Azure Foundry. The adapter is explicitly documented as a mandatory dependency. Two separate issues (both open, with 2 comments on one) independently report the same root cause. pip install fails with ResolutionImpossible. Workaround requires downgrading to pre-release versions, blocking access to all GA features.

source_issues.title: Python: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 incompatible with agent-framework-core 1.0.1 GA
source_issues.evidence: pip install fails with ResolutionImpossible due to conflicting version constraints: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 depends on agent-framework-core<=1.0.0rc3, but GA packages require >=1.0.1. Blocks adoption of agent-framework-foundry, GA features, and updated env var conventions (FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT, FOUNDRY_MODEL). Workaround requires staying on pre-release versions.

source_issues.title: Python: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework adapter does not yet support Agent Framework GA (1.0.0) — blocks hosted agent deployments
source_issues.evidence: Adapter is explicitly listed as a required dependency in Hosted Agents documentation for Python. Without it, agents cannot be wrapped as HTTP services for local testing or containerized deployment. The GA release (1.0.0) of the core framework is incompatible with the latest adapter (1.0.0b17).

signals.topic: CopilotStudioAgent unconditionally overwrites session on every run(), breaking multi-turn chat and memory
signals.summary: CopilotStudioAgent._run_impl and _run_stream_impl unconditionally set session.service_session_id to a new conversation ID on every call, even when the caller passes a persistent AgentSession. This means the Copilot Studio service has no memory of prior turns, making multi-turn chat impossible.
signals.review_reason: Core conversational workflow is broken: users cannot maintain multi-turn chat sessions with CopilotStudioAgent, which is a primary use case. The agent loses all context between run() calls. Clear code location identified with exact line of bug. No public-API workaround exists.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: CopilotStudioAgent creates a new conversation on every run(), ignoring the session= parameter
source_issues.evidence: Unconditional assignment `session.service_session_id = await self._start_new_conversation()` in _run_impl and _run_stream_impl overwrites the persistent session on every call. Reproducer shows agent forgets user name after one turn. No workaround exists within the public API.

signals.topic: Custom Executor in Workflow clears previous agent messages from workflow session context
signals.summary: After adding a custom Executor to a Workflow, its invocation clears previous agent messages from the workflow session, making downstream agents lose access to prior conversation history.
aliases: custom executor erases workflow message history
signals.review_reason: Custom executors in workflow chains cause message history loss for downstream agents, breaking multi-step agent orchestration workflows. Reproducer shows the exact messages lost when a custom executor is added. Users must remove custom executors as a workaround, defeating the purpose of extensibility.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Executor clears up previous agents messages from workflow context
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows a chain of 4 agents where ContextAgent4 can see all prior messages only when the custom upper_case executor is removed from the chain. With the executor in place, ContextAgent4 sees only its own preceding message. Output demonstrates exact message loss. Package versions: agent-framework-core 1.0.1.

signals.topic: Compaction generates colliding message IDs during incremental processing, breaking SummarizationStrategy and downstream consumers
signals.summary: _ensure_message_ids in _compaction.py assigns IDs using positional index on slices of the message list. When annotate_message_groups calls group_messages on slices, successive incremental compaction calls assign the same IDs (msg_0, msg_1, etc.) to different messages, causing duplicate IDs in the full history.
aliases: message ID collision in SlidingWindowStrategy compaction
signals.review_reason: Message ID collision corrupts conversation history for any agent using CompactionProvider with incremental compaction. The SummarizationStrategy is directly broken as it relies on non-unique message_ids to derive group IDs. Data corruption is confirmed with a reproducer. This affects all compaction strategies (SlidingWindowStrategy, etc.).

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Colliding Ids are assigned to message history creating issues when using compaction
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer output shows msg_1 and msg_2 assigned to multiple distinct messages. Downstream consumers (SummarizationStrategy._group_id_for) derive group_id from message_id, so colliding IDs collapse distinct groups into one, corrupting conversation summarization. Package agent-core-framework 1.0.1. Workaround requires adding unique IDs externally.

signals.topic: A2AAgent discards metadata from TaskArtifactUpdateEvent and other event types, causing silent data loss
signals.summary: The A2AAgent correctly processes metadata from A2AMessage parts, but fails to process metadata from Artifact, Message, Task, TaskStatusUpdateEvent, and TaskArtifactUpdateEvent types. Server-transmitted metadata is silently dropped for these event types.
aliases: A2AAgent metadata dropped in task events
signals.review_reason: A2AAgent silently drops server-side metadata for multiple event types. Any A2A client relying on metadata from these events (e.g., custom tracking, server-side annotations) will experience silent data loss with no error. This breaks interoperability with A2A-compliant servers that communicate important state via metadata fields.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Python A2AAgent Implementation Currently Ignores Metadata in TaskArtifactUpdateEvent
source_issues.evidence: A2AAgent processes metadata of Parts but ignores metadata for Artifact, Message, Task, TaskStatusUpdateEvent, and TaskArtifactUpdateEvent types. Server-side metadata is silently dropped. Package: agent-framework-a2a==1.0.0b260409.

signals.topic: MagenticOneGroupChat loses conversation context after user handoff in Human-in-the-Loop workflows
signals.summary: When using MagenticOneGroupChat with HandoffTermination to implement Human-in-the-Loop, the conversation context is completely lost after the handoff to the user. The orchestrator restarts the workflow from scratch instead of resuming from the preserved state, treating user input as a new request. This breaks the primary HitL workflow pattern advertised in official documentation.
aliases: Human-in-the-Loop context not preserved after handoff
signals.review_reason: Confirmed functional bug: HitL context loss after user handoff blocks the primary documented workflow for human-in-the-loop with MagenticOneGroupChat. The issue provides complete reproduction code, comparative evidence showing RoundRobinGroupChat works correctly, and references the official documentation that promises this behavior. State loss mid-session directly violates documented contract. Count=1 due to single-repo nature, so P1 rather than P0.

source_issues.title: Human-in-the-Loop with `MagenticOneGroupChat` loses context after handoff to user
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction code. MagenticOneGroupChat restarts workflow after user handoff instead of resuming. RoundRobinGroupChat preserves context in identical setup, proving the behavior is inconsistent. Documentation explicitly describes HandoffTermination as the mechanism for saving/resuming team state.

signals.topic: RoundRobinGroupChat raises raw Python exceptions (AttributeError/TypeError) instead of clear validation errors for invalid participant input
signals.summary: When RoundRobinGroupChat receives invalid participant arguments (None, non-sequence, list with non-agent objects), it raises low-level Python AttributeError or TypeError from internal implementation details instead of a clear user-facing validation error. This forces users to debug internal implementation details rather than understanding what went wrong.
aliases: poor error handling for invalid participants
signals.review_reason: Confirmed UX/DX bug: invalid participant inputs produce opaque Python exceptions rather than actionable validation errors. Three specific failure cases documented with exact error messages. These are described as 'realistic user mistakes' that directly degrade the debugging experience during development. While count=1 and single-repo, the user impact is clear and well-evidenced, warranting P1.

source_issues.title: RoundRobinGroupChat raises raw AttributeError/TypeError for invalid participants instead of a clear validation error
source_issues.evidence: Bug report documents three concrete invalid input scenarios (None, string, list with invalid items) each producing opaque Python errors (AttributeError, TypeError) rather than descriptive validation messages. Issue explicitly describes these as 'realistic user mistakes' and requests clear TypeError/ValueError with specific guidance on expected input types.

signals.topic: Playwright VSCode extension fails to discover tests and crashes with 'Illegal argument' errors
signals.summary: VSCode extension cannot find any tests, shows 'no tests have been found' in Testing tab, displays connect ETIMEDOUT errors in the editor, and crashes with 'Illegal argument: character must be non-negative' in the console — while CLI works perfectly fine. Trace viewer also renders blank snapshots for Angular/Ionic and Stencil.js frameworks.
signals.review_reason: 4 users report VSCode extension test discovery failing completely (blocking primary IDE workflow), with crashes and connection errors. Separately, trace viewer snapshots render blank for Angular/Ionic and Stencil.js frameworks — breaking the core debugging workflow. These are not edge cases: test discovery and trace viewing are core user workflows, and failures are reproducible in clean projects. P0 warranted due to high frequency (count=4) and main flow impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: PlayWright extension for VSCode showing 'no tests have been found'
source_issues.evidence: VSCode extension fails to load tests, shows connect ETIMEDOUT errors, crashes with 'Illegal argument: character must be non-negative'. CLI works correctly. Reproducible in clean project. Disabling extension removes the error.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer not displaying elements for Angular + Ionic app
source_issues.evidence: Trace viewer snapshot/preview is blank — page content not displayed in Action/Before/After sections for Angular + Ionic apps. Test passes but trace is unusable for debugging.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: Trace viewer shows horizontal scrollbar
source_issues.evidence: Regression since v1.59: trace.playwright.dev shows unwanted horizontal scrollbar due to extra timeline value in top right corner.

source_issues.title: Trace viewer snapshot is blank for content inside Stencil.js synthetic-shadow host elements
source_issues.evidence: Trace viewer renders blank page body for Stencil.js apps even though test passes and browser renders content correctly.

signals.topic: Firefox cannot read response JSON body for GET requests — blocks API testing in Firefox
signals.summary: Firefox 146 in v1.58.0 throws 'Protocol error (Network.getResponseBody): Component returned failure code: 0x80004005' when trying to read response.json() on GET requests. Firefox also ignores screen context options entirely, unlike Chromium and WebKit.
signals.review_reason: Firefox response body reading failure completely blocks API testing workflows in Firefox. Firefox screen context option failure is a separate Firefox-specific defect. Both affect Firefox users doing cross-browser testing, with clear reproduction evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Firefox 146 in v1.58.0 can't read response json body from GET requests
source_issues.evidence: Firefox 146 fails to read response.json() with Protocol error. Users cannot perform API testing in Firefox at all.

source_issues.title: Firefox: screen context option has no effect
source_issues.evidence: Firefox ignores contextOptions.screen entirely — drops the value and ties screen to viewport. Chromium and WebKit both work correctly. Users relying on screen context for responsive testing are blocked.

signals.topic: Proxy server CLI argument is silently ignored in MCP server — traffic bypasses configured proxy
signals.summary: The --proxy-server CLI argument is accepted without error but never applied to the browser launch. Chrome launches without the proxy flag, so all traffic bypasses the configured proxy entirely with no warning.
signals.review_reason: Silent failure on a security-critical feature (proxy configuration). User expects traffic to route through a proxy but it doesn't — without any error or warning. This is a deceptive failure mode: the tool appears to work but completely fails to provide the configured behavior.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: --proxy-server CLI arg is silently ignored — proxy never reaches Chrome launch arguments
source_issues.evidence: MCP server accepts --proxy-server without error but Chrome launches without --proxy-server in process arguments. All traffic bypasses the configured proxy silently — no error, no warning. Critical for users relying on proxy for security/testing.

signals.topic: Proxy authentication causes redirect hangs in Chromium — OAuth and login flows block indefinitely
signals.summary: Using Chromium with proxy credentials (username/password) causes redirects (302/303) to hang indefinitely. OAuth flows and standard login redirects are completely blocked.
signals.review_reason: Proxy auth is a common enterprise/testing setup and redirect hangs are a complete workflow blocker for OAuth, SSO, and login flows. Reproducible across multiple versions, affecting a core automation scenario.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Proxy auth without page.route() causes redirects to hang in Chromium
source_issues.evidence: Chromium launched with proxy credentials hangs on any redirect (302/303). OAuth flows and login redirects are completely blocked. Reproducible since v1.57.0 through v1.60.0-next.

signals.topic: Context cookies not sent with page.request.get() — forces manual workaround boilerplate
signals.summary: page.request.get() does not automatically include context-level cookies. Users must manually extract and attach cookies via headers, which is unintuitive and forces boilerplate code.
signals.review_reason: Unexpected behavior that forces manual workaround boilerplate. Degrades DX for API testing workflows where authenticated requests are needed. Not blocking but causes friction for users expecting context-level state to flow into page.request.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Context cookies not sent when using page.request.get()
source_issues.evidence: page.request.get() does not send context cookies. User must manually extract cookies and attach via Cookie header. This is unintuitive — page.request should inherit the page context's authenticated state.

signals.topic: Gemini 模型使用 developer role 时报 API 错误，SK 未做抽象层兼容处理
signals.summary: 用户在使用 Gemini 模型时使用 developer role，收到 'Gemini API doesn't support author role: developer' 错误。SK 作为跨模型抽象层未做角色转换兼容，导致用户在主流程中直接受阻。
signals.review_reason: 用户在实际使用 Gemini 时遭遇明确阻断性错误（API 不支持 developer role），且同一问题被 2 个独立 issue 报告（其中 1 个已 closed 为 duplicate）。SK 定位为跨模型抽象层，应处理不同模型的角色语义差异。此错误直接导致特定 Gemini agent 场景不可用，属于主流程阻断性痛点，满足 P0 条件。

source_issues.title: New Feature: Support Gemini Developer role
source_issues.evidence: 用户收到 'Gemini API doesn't support author role: developer' 错误，直接阻断 Gemini 的 developer role 使用场景

source_issues.title: New Feature: Gemini API doesn't support author role: developer
source_issues.evidence: duplicate issue — same error message, same user-facing blocking scenario

signals.topic: .NET chat/completions 调用后模型未返回 reasoning 内容（截图证据）
signals.summary: 用户在 .NET 环境下调用 chat/completions API 时，模型未返回 reasoning 相关内容，附有截图证据，4 条评论讨论。
signals.review_reason: 有明确 bug 报告和截图证据，comments 中有 4 条讨论说明其他用户也在关注该问题。虽然 count=1，但涉及 .NET 主流程（chat/completions），属于核心功能异常。定为 P1 而非 P0 因 count 未达到 P0 的 3 条阈值，但用户影响明确（reasoning 功能缺失）。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: chat/completions no reasoning
source_issues.evidence: 附截图显示 chat/completions 无 reasoning 内容返回，4 条评论讨论该 bug

signals.topic: HandoffOrchestration 在 agent 之间传递时产生不完整的摘要响应而非原始内容
signals.summary: HandoffOrchestration 在多 agent 交接场景下，将 agent 返回的完整内容摘要化，导致关键信息丢失，用户收到的响应不完整。
signals.review_reason: 多 agent 编排场景下，handoff 产生不完整响应是主流程功能降级问题。用户提供了完整 repro 代码和明确的问题描述（agent 返回完整信息但 orchestration 摘要化），4 条 comments 说明受到社区关注。虽 count=1，但属于核心 agent 编排功能的已知 bug，对多 agent 场景有明确影响。

source_issues.title: .Net Agent Orchestration: Incomplete response for HandoffOrchestration
source_issues.evidence: 示例代码展示 agent 返回完整历史信息，但 HandoffOrchestration 仅返回摘要，失去关键内容；4 条评论讨论该问题

signals.topic: Review panel 'Last turn' shows only one file instead of all files updated in the last assistant turn
signals.summary: The Review panel's 'Last turn' section incompletely reports changed files, showing only one file when multiple files were actually modified in a single turn.
aliases: Review panel incomplete file list last turn
signals.review_reason: Code review workflow is degraded: users cannot trust the Review panel to show all changes from the last turn, potentially hiding incomplete or incorrect work. Two independent reports confirm this is a reproducible bug, not an edge case. Files are updated on disk so no data loss, but Review panel is unreliable for code review.

source_issues.title: Review panel 'Last turn' does not show all files updated in the last turn
source_issues.evidence: Last turn updated both privacyassistant.py and js-process-individual-tickets/privacyassistant.js. Review panel only showed js-process-individual-tickets/privacyassistant.js. Files were actually updated on disk; issue is in what Review panel includes for last turn.

source_issues.title: Review panel 'Last turn' does not show all files updated in the last turn
source_issues.evidence: After a turn that updated multiple files, Review panel 'Last turn' section only showed one of them. Files were actually updated on disk; the issue appears to be in what the Review panel includes for the last turn.

signals.topic: Codex TUI crashes when skills/list request fails behind corporate proxy (returns HTML instead of JSON)
signals.summary: Corporate proxies intercept HTTPS requests to chatgpt.com and return HTML warning pages instead of JSON. The TUI crashes fatally instead of degrading gracefully, making the app unusable in such environments.
signals.review_reason: Reproducible fatal crash preventing app startup in corporate proxy environments. TUI exits completely instead of degrading gracefully. Specific root cause identified in code (AppCommandView::ListSkills uses ? operator that crashes on proxy HTML response). Workflow-blocking: user cannot use Codex at all behind such proxies.

source_issues.title: TUI crashes when skills/list fails behind corporate proxy
source_issues.evidence: Corporate proxy returns HTML via 302 redirect; reqwest follows redirect, receives HTML, JSON parsing fails with 'expected value at line 1 column 1', error bubbles up via '?' operator causing fatal TUI exit. Startup path already handles this gracefully with match+warn, but skills refresh path does not.

signals.topic: Review pane on Windows Codex Desktop shows 'Loading diff' indefinitely due to malformed /D:/ path prefix in git diff command
signals.summary: Codex Desktop constructs invalid git diff pathspecs (/D:/...) on Windows, causing the Review pane diff view to be permanently stuck.
signals.review_reason: Key Codex feature (Review pane for viewing code changes) is completely non-functional on Windows. Specific git path construction bug identified (absolute drive path incorrectly prefixed with /). Workflow-blocking for Windows desktop users who rely on the Review pane.

source_issues.title: Review pane stuck on 'Loading diff' on Windows due to invalid git diff path (/D:/...)
source_issues.evidence: Codex Desktop invokes 'git diff -- /D:/<repo>/src/client/styles/global.css' which fails with 'fatal: Invalid path /D:: No such file or directory'. The same diff works with repo-relative paths. git status and git diff --stat work fine. Only the Codex Desktop diff invocation with absolute /D:/ paths fails. Review pane is effectively unusable on Windows for changed files.

signals.topic: apply_patch still requests approval despite workspace-write trust level configured
signals.summary: When workspace is configured with workspace-write + untrusted trust level, Codex still prompts for approval when applying patches, even though writing to the workspace should be permitted under that configuration.
signals.review_reason: File editing workflow is interrupted by unnecessary approval prompts despite correct trust configuration. User-perceived as broken promise of workspace-write permission level. Each file edit requires manual intervention, degrading UX significantly for iterative workflows.

source_issues.title: apply_patch still requires approval in workspace-write + untrusted (Ubuntu 24.04, v0.120.0)
source_issues.evidence: /status shows 'Custom (workspace-write, untrusted)'. User asks Codex to create dummy.txt via apply_patch; patch preview appears and Codex still asks 'Would you like to make the following edits?'. Expected: no prompt since workspace-write should permit file writes. codex sandbox linux -- /bin/true succeeds, confirming sandbox is working. sandbox_mode='none' is NOT set, so this is a policy evaluation bug, not a sandbox misconfiguration.

signals.topic: apply_patch fails on Ubuntu 25.10 due to nested bwrap sandbox namespace conflict
signals.summary: On Ubuntu 25.10, apply_patch fails because Codex is already running inside a bwrap sandbox and the patch tool attempts to create additional namespaces that fail with EPERM, blocking file editing entirely.
signals.review_reason: File editing is completely blocked on Ubuntu 25.10 due to nested sandbox namespace conflict. Direct shell writes work, confirming filesystem is accessible. Root cause is specific to nested bwrap on AppArmor-restricted environments. Workflow-blocking for Ubuntu 25.10 users who cannot use apply_patch.

source_issues.title: `apply_patch` fails inside sandbox on Ubuntu 25.10 due to nested `bwrap` namespace error
source_issues.evidence: Codex already running with bwrap arguments (--unshare-user --unshare-pid --unshare-net --apply-seccomp-then-exec). apply_patch triggers another bwrap which fails with 'bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted'. Direct shell writes in same repo succeed. Kernel namespace settings are correct. Workaround: setting sandbox_mode='none' for the repo avoids the issue. Error log: codex_core::tools::router error={'output':'bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted'}. Exit code 1.

signals.topic: Legacy MCP import errors (MCPServer, MCPServerSse) block agent initialization for users on older package versions
signals.summary: Users encounter ImportError when trying to import MCPServer or MCPServerSse from agents.mcp on specific SDK versions, preventing agent initialization entirely. Two distinct import names affected (MCPServer and MCPServerSse), both blocking the MCP integration setup flow.
signals.review_reason: ImportError at startup blocks the entire MCP integration flow, which is a core SDK feature. Two distinct import names are affected (count=2). These are legacy issues (April 2025) that remained unresolved, indicating users may still encounter this on certain version/install combinations. The error is a complete agent initialization failure with no workaround mentioned.

source_issues.title: ImportError: cannot import name 'MCPServer' from 'agents.mcp'
source_issues.evidence: User encounter ImportError when importing MCPServer from agents.mcp on latest SDK version with fresh venv. Full traceback: ImportError: cannot import name 'MCPServer' from 'agents.mcp'.

source_issues.title: ImportError: cannot import name 'MCPServerSse' from 'agents.mcp'

signals.topic: OpenAI /v1/responses endpoint silently hangs 10–28% of concurrent requests with no timeout or SDK retry

Affected requests hang indefinitely (up to 60s) until caller-side timeout kills them. Both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK Runner.run() are affected at identical rates, confirming the issue is in the OpenAI API server, not the SDK.

While the root cause is in the OpenAI API server (not the SDK), the impact is 100% on SDK users and represents a critical production failure pattern.

signals.topic: AsyncResponses.parse() causes unbounded memory leak via Pydantic schema rebuild accumulation
signals.summary: When using AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models and free TypeVars, pydantic's model_rebuild always fails due to unresolved TypeVar, causing a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust object) to be allocated on every call. These accumulate without bound, leading to linear RSS growth and eventual OOM in long-running servers.
aliases: Pydantic TypeVar schema rebuild memory leak responses.parse()
signals.review_reason: This is a critical user pain point: it causes unbounded memory growth in long-running server processes, with concrete evidence (flame graph, detailed root cause with call stack). The leak is confirmed to be in the library code path (openai/lib/_parsing/_responses.py) and will eventually OOM any production server making repeated structured output calls. The severity meets P0 despite count=1 due to the catastrophic impact (process death) and concrete evidence.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: User provides flame graph evidence and detailed root cause analysis: TextFormatT is an unresolved free TypeVar, model_rebuild always returns False, MockCoreSchema._built_memo never populated, causing unbounded SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer allocation on every responses.parse() call. signals.topic: AsyncCompletions.parse() memory leak with dynamic Pydantic create_model

signals.topic: Web publish form crashes when uploading plugin folders containing extensionless executable files
signals.summary: When a user drags and drops a plugin folder with extensionless executable files (e.g. shell scripts without .sh extension), the web publish form sends an empty Content-Type header because file.type is an empty string and the ?? operator does not fall through. This causes Convex to reject the upload with 400 BadHeader, making the entire publish workflow fail for any plugin with hook scripts or other extensionless binaries in bin/. The workaround (zipping first) is non-obvious and changes the user workflow.
aliases: web upload fails for extensionless executables
signals.review_reason: The web publish form is a primary publishing path for the platform. The crash is systematic for any plugin containing extensionless executables (a common pattern for hook scripts). The bug is precisely identified and reproducible. The workaround of zipping changes the intended UX (drag-drop folder). Count=1 with documented root cause, reproduction steps, and workaround analysis.

source_issues.title: Package publish fails with BadHeader when uploading extensionless executables
source_issues.evidence: User provides full root cause analysis: the ?? operator in uploadUtils.ts does not fall through for empty string file.type, resulting in Content-Type='' which Convex rejects as 400 BadHeader. Reproducible in Chrome 146 on Linux. User identifies the exact affected code path in src/routes/upload/-utils.ts and src/lib/uploadUtils.ts. Workaround of zipping is documented but is non-obvious UX. CLI is not affected (different code path using mime.getType).

signals.topic: Windows: ollama launch openclaw creates duplicate gateway when gateway runs as Scheduled Task (Session 0 isolation)
signals.summary: On Windows, running `ollama launch openclaw` while the OpenClaw Gateway is already running as a Scheduled Task (Session 0) spawns a second node.exe process that also binds to port 18789. User-session processes cannot enumerate Session 0 processes, so the launch integration fails to detect the existing gateway. This causes mDNS name conflicts, RPC probe failures, EPERM file-access errors on shared state files, and handshake/close WebSocket errors.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-reported Windows-specific bug that causes duplicate gateway processes, port conflicts, mDNS name collisions, and file-access EPERM errors. The root cause (Windows Session 0 isolation preventing user-session process enumeration) is a genuine architectural pain that can block the gateway from functioning normally. The user provided clear reproduction steps and multiple observable failure symptoms, confirming active user impact.
