source_issues.evidence: Agent called WebSearch (not registered) 754 times across 434 assistant messages. 3.57M input tokens consumed, ~$70 estimated API cost, zero useful output. Any misconfigured tool causes unbounded token consumption.

signals.topic: Gateway virtual memory bloat (22GB+ VIRT) at startup with no proportional RSS — affects memory-constrained environments
signals.summary: Immediately after Gateway startup, VIRT reaches 22GB+ (VmPeak: 23.7GB) while RSS stays normal (~380MB). This is caused by Node.js V8 ArrayBufferAllocator or native module loading, not by actual workload. Affects users on memory-constrained systems, shared hosting, or environments with container memory limits.
aliases: Gateway high VIRT RSS mismatch at startup
signals.review_reason: Causes crashes or OOM kills on memory-constrained environments (shared hosting, containers, low-RAM VPS). VIRT bloat of 22GB+ can trigger system-level OOM even though RSS is normal, because some container/cgroup accounting looks at virtual size. Affects system stability in resource-limited deployments. Previously reported (#6413, closed as 'not planned') and persists.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Massive virtual memory bloat (22GB+ VIRT) immediately after Gateway startup, identical to previously reported issue #6413
source_issues.evidence: VmPeak: 23.7GB, VmSize: 23.7GB, VmRSS: ~380MB (normal). ~1300 memory mappings (vs normal 100-200). Affects users on memory-limited systems; only RSS protection via systemd MemoryMax works as workaround. Reproduced across multiple Node.js versions. Regression from #6413.

signals.topic: Subagent sessions silently lose QMD memory search — FTS/hybrid recall fails with 4s timeout fallback to MEMORY.md
signals.summary: Subagent sessions spawned via sessions_spawn cannot use qmd memory search because session keys resolve to channel=unknown, chatType=unknown, triggering default-deny policy. QMD search times out after 4s then falls back to builtin index — a silent degradation users only notice by tailing gateway.err.log.
aliases: QMD FTS fallback in subagent sessions
signals.review_reason: Subagent sessions lose critical memory search functionality silently. Users relying on QMD (full-text search, ranked results) in subagent workflows get degraded results with no indication of failure. The 4s timeout creates perceptible latency. This is a key functionality degradation affecting a core workflow (persistent subagents with memory).

source_issues.title: qmd scope denies subagent sessions — channel/chatType resolve to undefined
source_issues.evidence: Subagent sessions lose qmd memory search (FTS + hybrid recall). 4s timeout per search before fallback. Cross-workspace recall, ranked results, and chunk-level hits unavailable. Silent failure: user only notices latency, not capability loss. Only visible via gateway.err.log.

signals.topic: WhatsApp Dispatch 连接后无法处理/响应消息（核心功能完全失效）
signals.summary: 用户配置 WhatsApp Dispatch 后，状态显示已连接（绿色在线），消息在手机上标记为已读，但 Open Interpreter Desktop UI 完全没有响应，不触发任何代码执行也不回复消息。消息处理管道完全中断。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1 不足以达到 P0 高频标准，但该 issue 描述了一个关键功能（WhatsApp Dispatch）的完全失效：消息处理管道从读取消息到触发 LLM 执行到回复的整条链路全部中断。这不是边缘体验问题，而是核心集成功能的阻断性失效。状态显示在线但功能完全不工作，构成明确的用户可感知痛点，定级 P1。

source_issues.title: WhatsApp Dispatch connected but not processing or sending messages windows
source_issues.evidence: WhatsApp 状态显示 'Connected'（绿色），消息在手机上显示已读（蓝色双勾），但 Open Interpreter Desktop UI 停留在 'What would you like to work on?' 界面，完全无响应，不执行代码也不回复。连接状态与实际功能完全脱节。

signals.topic: Uncaught OSError crashes in util.py line 1054 causing aider to fail on startup
signals.summary: Multiple users encounter uncaught OSError at util.py line 1054, crashing aider immediately on launch with no graceful error handling.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users hitting the same uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054, both resulting in aider startup failure. The crash is unhandled, providing no user-friendly error message. Count=2 is borderline for P0, but lack of a sample URL with full traceback (body is null) reduces confidence in P0. Marked P1 due to startup-blocking nature with repeat occurrence.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught exception at util.py line 1054 causing aider to crash. Body null but title confirms crash.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught OSError in same file and line. Different author from 5030. Confirms systemic uncaught exception in util.py.

signals.topic: UnicodeEncodeError crash on Windows when console charset cannot encode special characters
signals.summary: On Windows with cp1251 locale, running the /map command causes an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError that crashes aider completely, as the console's charmap codec cannot encode Unicode characters like \u22ee.
aliases: charmap codec can't encode character crash
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow block on Windows: the /map command (core navigation feature) crashes aider entirely due to unhandled Unicode encoding. The error propagates through multiple exception handlers without being caught. Affects any Windows user with a non-UTF8 console encoding (cp1251 and similar). Though count=1, the impact is severe (full crash), the root cause is well-understood from the traceback, and the feature (/map) is a primary navigation tool in aider.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1251.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback shows UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u22ee' on Windows cp1251. Crash occurs when running /map command, completely blocking that workflow. Python 3.12.7, Windows 10.

signals.topic: TypeError crash at startup when git working tree directory cannot be resolved
signals.summary: Aider crashes on startup with TypeError in pathlib.py because Path receives None instead of a valid path string, triggered when git working tree directory cannot be resolved.
signals.review_reason: Aider completely fails to start due to uncaught TypeError from Path(None). This is a startup blocker — users cannot use aider at all. The root cause is git working tree directory resolving to None, which should be handled gracefully with a clear error message. Marked P1 (not P0) because count=1 and only one affected repo.

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in pathlib.py line 373
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback: TypeError: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'NoneType'. Crash occurs during GitRepo initialization in main.py before aider even starts. Linux, Python 3.12.8.

signals.topic: PermissionError crash at startup when .aider cache directory cannot be created
signals.summary: On startup, aider attempts to create /app/.aider/caches and crashes with PermissionError when the parent directory cannot be written, blocking the entire application.
aliases: PermissionError creating .aider cache directory startup crash
signals.review_reason: Startup blocker: aider crashes with PermissionError when attempting to create its cache directory. While the immediate error is permission-related, the deeper issue is that aider does not gracefully handle this failure scenario — it should either use an alternate cache location or provide a clear user-facing error. Count=1, P1 due to non-P0 single-incident rule.

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1311
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/app/.aider'. Crash occurs during version check at startup before aider is usable. Linux in containerized environment.

signals.topic: ModuleNotFoundError crash when using web URL scraping feature without playwright installed
signals.summary: When attempting to scrape web content via the /web command, aider crashes with ModuleNotFoundError if playwright is not installed, with no graceful fallback or user-friendly error message.
aliases: playwright module missing web scraping crash
signals.review_reason: The /web command (core feature for fetching URL content) crashes with uncaught ModuleNotFoundError instead of either installing playwright automatically or providing a clear error message telling the user to install it. This blocks an important workflow feature. Count=1, P1.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in scrape.py line 134
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright' when running /web command. Crash occurs during URL content scraping. Windows 10, Python 3.9.25, no virtual environment.

signals.topic: Web UI eval crashes with circular JSON error when using external LLM providers as llm-rubric judge
signals.summary: Running eval from the Web UI with Bedrock or Anthropic providers as llm-rubric judge throws a 'Converting circular structure to JSON' error, completely blocking eval execution in the UI. The same config works correctly via CLI.
aliases: web UI eval crash with LLM judge provider
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug in the Web UI. Users cannot run evals with LLM-judge providers from the UI at all, while the exact same config works via CLI. This constitutes a critical UI-to-backend communication failure affecting the primary evaluation interface.

source_issues.title: Converting circular structure to JSON when using Bedrock provider as llm-rubric judge in UI
source_issues.evidence: Web UI throws 'TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON' when using Bedrock or Anthropic provider as llm-rubric judge. The eval never executes. Works in CLI. Affects both AWS SDK and Anthropic SDK clients which contain circular references that break JSON.stringify during UI-to-worker communication.

signals.topic: promptfoo redteam discover command fails with 'Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery' backend error
signals.summary: The promptfoo redteam discover command sends an unrecognized task type to the promptfoo.app backend API, causing every invocation to fail with HTTP 400. The same credentials and config work for redteam generate.
signals.review_reason: The redteam discover command is a documented feature that fails 100% of the time with an HTTP 400 from the backend. This is a complete functional break of a named CLI command, preventing users from running security red-teaming discovery workflows.

source_issues.title: `promptfoo redteam discover` fails with `Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery`
source_issues.evidence: Every invocation of `promptfoo redteam discover` returns HTTP 400 with 'Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery'. Same credentials and endpoint work for `redteam generate`. The command is completely non-functional as documented.

signals.topic: anthropic:messages provider does not support apiKeyRequired: false, blocking Claude Code users from using llm-rubric
signals.summary: The anthropic:messages provider (used as default grader for llm-rubric) requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Claude Pro/Max subscribers using Claude Code cannot use llm-rubric without purchasing separate API credits.
aliases: Claude Code session auth not supported for messages provider
llm-rubric requires API key for Claude Code users
signals.review_reason: While only 1 issue, this blocks a core evaluation feature (llm-rubric) for a large class of users (Claude Code subscribers without API keys). The workaround of using keyword matching assertions loses semantic evaluation capability, which is a significant functional degradation.

source_issues.title: Allow anthropic:messages provider to authenticate via Claude Code session (apiKeyRequired: false)
source_issues.evidence: Users with active Claude Code sessions (Claude Pro/Max subscribers) cannot use llm-rubric for evaluations because anthropic:messages requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. They must purchase additional API credits. The anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider already supports apiKeyRequired: false.

signals.topic: g-eval assertion silently fails with NaN score and empty reason when value is empty array
signals.summary: handleGEval returns NaN for both score and pass when the value array is empty, producing a silent false-fail with no actionable feedback. Users cannot diagnose why their assertion failed.
aliases: empty value array causes g-eval to return NaN
signals.review_reason: Silent failure with no error message is a significant UX issue for evaluation assertions. Users see a FAIL result with NaN and empty text, making diagnosis impossible without reading source code. This constitutes a confusing experience that can block evaluation workflows.

source_issues.title: bug: handleGEval returns NaN score and silent false-fail when value is an empty array
source_issues.evidence: When renderedValue is an empty array, g-eval computes 0/0 resulting in NaN. The assertion fails silently with score: NaN and an empty reason string. No actionable error message is shown to the user.

signals.topic: GET /eval/:id/table endpoint crashes with RangeError for large evals due to V8 string length limit
signals.summary: The eval table web UI endpoint throws an unhandled RangeError when JSON payload exceeds V8's ~512MB string limit, preventing large evals (with base64 images or large prompts) from loading in the UI.
aliases: large eval results crash web UI
signals.review_reason: Users running image-based or large-scale evals cannot view their results in the web UI at all. This blocks a core workflow (reviewing eval results) for a specific but realistic use case. The issue is still open, indicating it may not be fully resolved.

source_issues.title: RangeError crash on GET /eval/:id/table for large evals
source_issues.evidence: Endpoint returns HTTP 500 when eval payload exceeds V8's ~512MB JSON.stringify limit. Triggered by large outputs, base64-encoded images, or many test cases. UI fails to load results. Issue is open (unfixed).

signals.topic: Azure AI Search 集成中 falsy 值被静默存为 None，数据丢失
signals.summary: Azure AI Search vector store 将 falsy 值（0、空字符串、空列表）存储为 None，导致数据静默丢失；此外 Document Summary Index 与 Azure AI Search + Cosmos DB 组合使用时查询抛出 KeyError，两个问题均指向 Azure 集成中的元数据处理缺陷。
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均来自真实用户场景（Azure 全家桶集成），均造成数据丢失或主流程阻断：falsy 值变 None 是静默数据损坏，Document Summary Index 的 KeyError 使查询完全失败。两者根因均指向 Azure 集成层元数据处理的共性缺陷，高置信度。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: falsy metadata values stored as None in Azure AI Search index
source_issues.evidence: 创建含 metadata value=0 的节点，从 index 中检索后值变成 None；根因是代码用 'if metadata_value' 而非 'if metadata_value is not None'，所有 falsy 值均被错误覆盖。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Query failure with Document Summary Index using Azure AI Search and Cosmos DB
source_issues.evidence: 使用 Azure AI Search + Cosmos DB 时 Document Summary Index 查询抛出 KeyError: 'summary_id'，文档摘要映射被错误地存入 docstore 而非 index_store，导致主流程查询完全阻断。

signals.topic: 跨提供商 Agent 工作流中 tool_kwargs 未 JSON 序列化导致 OpenAI 400 错误
signals.summary: Anthropic LLM 作为编排器向 OpenAI LLM 子代理交接时，to_openai_message_dict 将 tool_kwargs(dict) 直接放入 function.arguments，OpenAI API 要求字符串格式，引发 BadRequestError 400，完全阻断跨提供商 Agent Workflow。
signals.review_reason: 清晰的阻断性 bug：跨提供商（Anthropic→OpenAI）Agent Workflow 触发 400 错误导致主流程失败，提供完整复现代码和对比修复方案，确认是遗漏的 json.dumps 序列化步骤。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs and breaks cross-provider agent workflows
source_issues.evidence: 当 Anthropic LLM 生成的 ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs 为 Python dict 时，to_openai_message_dict 直接放入 arguments 字段，OpenAI API 返回 400 BadRequestError: expected a string, got object。同一模式在 to_openai_responses_message_dict 中已正确处理（有 json.dumps），但 Chat Completions 路径遗漏了该修复。

signals.topic: vLLM 0.19+ 移除 best_of 参数导致 llama-index-llms-vllm 完全不可用
signals.summary: llama-index-llms-vllm 0.7.0 在 _model_kwargs 中无条件传入已移除的 best_of 参数，vLLM 0.19.0+ SamplingParams 拒绝该参数引发 TypeError，每次 .complete() 调用均失败，集成完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 版本兼容性导致的阻断性问题：用户升级 vLLM 后集成完全崩溃，每次调用都 TypeError，有多个用户反馈（4 comments），影响明确。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index-llms-vllm: best_of removed from vLLM SamplingParams causes TypeError on .complete()
source_issues.evidence: vLLM>=0.19.0 移除了 SamplingParams 的 best_of 参数，但 llama-index-llms-vllm 仍无条件传入，导致每次 .complete() 调用抛出 TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'best_of'，wrapper 完全不可用。有 4 条评论表明用户受影响。

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore.query() 同步路径静默忽略 metadata_keyword_suffix 参数
signals.summary: ElasticsearchStore.query() 的同步包装方法接收 metadata_keyword_suffix 参数但未传递给异步实现，导致自定义元数据后缀在同步路径下完全失效，查询使用默认 .keyword 后缀而用户无感知。
signals.review_reason: 静默参数忽略 bug：用户配置了自定义 metadata_keyword_suffix 但同步路径下完全不生效，查询行为与预期不符。虽然无异常抛出但导致错误的查询结果，影响同步检索场景。Issue 已关闭确认。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore.query() ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on the synchronous path
source_issues.evidence: 同步包装器的 query 方法将 metadata_keyword_suffix 传递给 **kwargs 但未显式转发到 aubquery()，自定义后缀在同步路径被静默忽略，没有异常仅结果错误。Issue 已由维护者关闭，确认了 bug 存在。

signals.topic: PDFReader 使用 S3 文件时 Path() 强制转换为 WindowsPath 导致 S3 文件加载失败
signals.summary: 使用 SimpleDirectoryReader + s3fs 读取 S3 中的 PDF 时，PDFReader.load_data() 无条件将路径强制转换为 Path 对象，Windows 环境下生成 WindowsPath 而非 PosixPath，导致 S3 路径格式错误引发 ValueError，PDF 完全无法加载。
aliases: S3 PDF loading Path casting WindowsPath
signals.review_reason: 阻断性 bug：S3 文件系统 + PDFReader 组合在 Windows 环境下完全无法工作（8 条讨论，标 P1），用户无法用 S3 中的 PDF 构建 RAG 应用，主流程失败。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: impossible to use PDFReader with an S3 file because of Path() casting
source_issues.evidence: 当 s3fs 与 PDFReader 配合使用时，Path(file) 在 Windows 上生成 WindowsPath 对象，s3fs.open() 因路径格式不对抛出 ValueError: Attempt to open non key-like path。Issue 有 8 条讨论，标为 P1，严重影响 S3 + PDF 使用场景。

signals.topic: Windows Codex MCP: first memory tool call crashes stdio transport, killing the entire MCP session
signals.summary: On Windows, the first real memory MCP tool call (memory_search/memory_store) after a successful mcp_status causes the stdio transport to close permanently, killing all subsequent claude-flow/* tool calls in the same session. The server starts fine and mcp_status succeeds, but the moment a memory operation triggers first-run initialization, the transport dies.
aliases: first memory tool call kills MCP transport on Windows
memory tools crash stdio transport on Windows
signals.review_reason: MCP memory tool is a primary workflow for Claude Code users. The first call permanently kills the stdio transport, making the entire MCP server unusable for the session. This is a complete flow failure for the memory use case on Windows, a major platform. Count=1 because only one issue explicitly documents this, but the evidence is strong (verified repro steps, clear stack trace path, known memory initialization flow difference between Windows and Linux).

source_issues.title: Windows Codex: first memory MCP tool call closes stdio transport after successful startup
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro: mcp_status succeeds, but memory_search immediately closes stdio transport and all subsequent calls fail. Server startup succeeds. Crash happens on first memory-tool call, not on registration. Active backend bootstraps storage under .swarm/memory.db, which differs from legacy .claude-flow/memory path.

signals.topic: Memory data stored via CLI is invisible to MCP tools and vice versa — two hardcoded storage paths split the dataset
signals.summary: The CLI 'memory store' command writes to .swarm/memory.db (SQLite) while the MCP tool path reads from .claude-flow/memory/store.json (legacy JSON). Data stored via one entry point is completely invisible to the other. The documented CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH env var is not honored by either code path.
aliases: memory CLI vs MCP storage path mismatch
memory data siloed between CLI and MCP entry points
signals.review_reason: This causes fundamental data inconsistency: users who store memory via CLI (e.g. in a workflow script) find that Claude Code's MCP memory tools cannot retrieve it, and vice versa. This breaks the core memory use case — a user-facing feature that silently returns empty results rather than surfacing an error. The count is 1 because the issue comprehensively documents both code paths, making it a single root cause with broad impact on memory operations.

source_issues.title: CLI and MCP memory tools write to different databases (.swarm/memory.db vs .claude-flow/memory/store.json)
source_issues.evidence: Two code paths hardcode different directory constants: MCP tools in memory-tools.ts resolve to '.claude-flow/memory/store.json'; memory initializer in memory-initializer.ts resolves to '.swarm/memory.db' (SQLite). Stored entries from CLI are completely absent when MCP tools search, and vice versa. The documented CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH env var is not read by either path.

signals.topic: init --skip-claude silently overwrites user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md without creating any backup
signals.summary: Despite documentation stating '--skip-claude: Skip .claude/ directory creation', running 'ruflo init --skip-claude --minimal' in any directory overwrites the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (Claude Code's global config) with a 4-line auto-generated stub, with no backup created. Labels confirm: bug, data-loss, installer, cli.
aliases: global Claude Code config overwritten by init command
no backup created before CLAUDE.md overwrite
signals.review_reason: This is unambiguous data loss: user content in a configuration file that controls Claude Code behavior is silently overwritten and unrecoverable without a backup. The --skip-claude flag name and documentation explicitly promise to not touch ~/.claude/, creating a false sense of safety. This is a design flaw with clear user impact, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: init --skip-claude overwrites ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md without backup
source_issues.evidence: Verified repro steps: user had 42 lines of custom workflow rules in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; after running 'ruflo init --skip-claude --minimal' in a sandbox directory, the file was overwritten with a 4-line stub. The --skip-claude flag documentation explicitly promises to leave .claude/ untouched. No backup was created. Labels include 'data-loss' and 'bug', confirming developer triage.

signals.topic: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() omits vectorBackend config, causing 8 controllers (including vectorBackend) to permanently fail
signals.summary: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() initializes AgentDB with only {dbPath}, omitting vectorBackend:'rvf'. AgentDB falls back to HNSWLib and does not expose a vectorBackend controller. This causes the vectorBackend controller and 7 dependent controllers (mutationGuard, gnnService, attestationLog, semanticRouter, guardedVectorBackend, rvfOptimizer, graphAdapter) to all report as failed, disabling core AI/reasoning features.
aliases: vectorBackend controller always null due to missing config
8 controllers cascade-fail due to missing vectorBackend config
signals.review_reason: Configuration bug causing 8 controllers to fail in cascade, disabling multiple AI/reasoning features. Count=1 with single-repo observation; downgraded to P1 because user impact may not be immediately obvious (controllers report as failed rather than a clear error message). Kept=true because the cascade to 7 additional controllers is a clear architectural defect with direct user-facing feature impact.

source_issues.title: Bug: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() does not pass vectorBackend config — AgentDB falls back to HNSWLib and vectorBackend controller always returns null
source_issues.evidence: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() at controller-registry.ts:498 calls new AgentDB({dbPath}) without vectorBackend, causing getController('vectorBackend') to return null. This marks vectorBackend as 'failed' and cascades to 7 additional controllers: mutationGuard, gnnService, attestationLog, semanticRouter, guardedVectorBackend, rvfOptimizer, graphAdapter. By contrast, AgentDBBackend in agentdb-backend.ts correctly passes the full config including vectorBackend.

signals.topic: MCP server unconditionally registers ~25 browser_* tools that always fail with ENOENT when agent-browser is not installed
signals.summary: The MCP server unconditionally registers ~25 browser_* tools (browser_open, browser_click, etc.) regardless of whether the agent-browser binary is installed. Each tool call throws spawnSync ENOENT since agent-browser is not on PATH. This wastes tool-use turns, creates confusing UX, and the model may attempt to use advertised-but-broken tools.
aliases: browser MCP tools always fail without agent-browser installed
ENOENT on browser_* tools when agent-browser binary absent
unconditional browser tool registration causes spurious failures
signals.review_reason: These tools are advertised to the model and always fail, wasting tool-use turns and degrading Claude Code's ability to use browser automation. While not a crash, this creates persistent negative UX and misleads the model about available capabilities. The fix is simple (add a PATH check before registration) but the impact is continuous for any user without agent-browser installed.

source_issues.title: Bug: browser_* MCP tools registered unconditionally — spawnSync agent-browser ENOENT
source_issues.evidence: mcp-client.ts:84 unconditionally spreads browserTools into the tool list. browser-tools.ts:26 calls execFileSync('agent-browser', ...) which throws ENOENT if not on PATH. Tools appear in Claude Code's tool list, causing the model to attempt calls that always fail with 'spawnSync agent-browser ENOENT'. Repro: install claude-flow without agent-browser, call browser_open, observe ENOENT error.

signals.topic: v0.24.1 regression: Chrome killed after ~7s idle due to PR_SET_PDEATHSIG + tokio thread recycling
signals.summary: v0.24.1 introduced PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in Chrome's pre_exec hook which causes Chrome to be killed after ~7-9 seconds of idle time on every site. This is a critical regression that breaks all automation workflows where commands are spaced >7s apart, including multi-step downloads and live preview streaming.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed P0 regression in v0.24.1 that causes Chrome to be silently killed after ~7s of idle on EVERY site. It blocks all automation workflows requiring >7s between commands (downloads, multi-step flows, live previews). Count=1 but review_reason provides explicit strong user impact evidence: 100% reproducible, validated fix provided, breaks core automation use cases.

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: Chrome exits after ~7-9s idle on every site, every page, in both headless and headed modes. Download workflows break after first download. Verified against v0.24.0 where it works fine. Reproduction is 100% reproducible with zero custom args. Fix validated by reporter with 15+ seconds idle, 5 downloads with 10s delays.

signals.topic: CDP connect hangs indefinitely when browser has discarded/frozen tabs (Memory Saver)
signals.summary: agent-browser --cdp <port> hangs forever when connecting to a browser with discarded/sleeping tabs, which is the default state on any daily browser due to Chrome's Memory Saver. The root cause is that Page.enable hangs forever on tabs without a renderer process, permanently blocking the daemon.
signals.review_reason: This issue renders the entire CDP connect feature unusable for any user connecting to their daily browser, which is the most common real-world use case. Chrome's Memory Saver discards tabs by default, making this a high-frequency blocker for all CDP users. The hang is indefinite (no timeout), making the feature completely unusable in its current state.

source_issues.title: Bug: CDP connect hangs on browsers with discarded/frozen tabs (Memory Saver)
source_issues.evidence: Out of 20 randomly sampled tabs on a daily browser, 14 timed out (discarded). Reproduced on both Brave and Chrome. signals.topic: Chrome fails to start on Linux containers/VMs due to sandbox restrictions with no workaround in Agent Dashboard UI

signals.review_reason: This blocks Chrome sessions entirely on Linux containers/VMs/CI environments which are extremely common for AI agent deployments. Without configurable launch flags, the Agent Dashboard is unusable in these environments. While there is a CLI workaround, the Agent Dashboard (the primary UI for non-technical users) provides no path to resolution.

Affects Docker containers, cloud VMs, CI runners, and hardened Linux hosts — extremely common environments for agent workflows.

signals.topic: invalid tool call input stored as raw string causes downstream API rejection
signals.summary: When tool call JSON parsing fails, the SDK stores the raw invalid string as input instead of a JSON object. This causes Amazon Bedrock (and other providers requiring JSONObject input) to reject the subsequent API call with a validation error, bypassing the tool-error recovery mechanism.
aliases: tool call JSON parse failure causes API rejection
signals.review_reason: Breaks the tool-error self-healing mechanism: when a tool call has invalid JSON input, the SDK generates a tool-error (correct behavior) but the raw string in input causes the API call itself to fail, so the model never gets to see or recover from the error. Root cause identified at parse-tool-call.ts line 82-83.

source_issues.title: Invalid tool call input stored as raw string causes API rejection on next step
source_issues.evidence: The SDK correctly marks the tool call as invalid and generates a tool-error, but the raw string input causes the next API call to fail with 'The format of the value at messages.X.content.Y.toolUse.input is invalid. Provide a json object' before the model can see the tool-error. Reproduction confirmed via middleware that corrupts tool-call chunks.

signals.topic: Malformed Origin header in Server Actions causes HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 400, enabling DoS attacks

A public DoS proof-of-concept is available. Three separate reports confirm the same root cause across Pages Router Server Actions.
signals.review_reason: HTTP 500 is a critical server availability failure. Any malformed Origin header (bots, proxies, reflected XSS) causes all users of a self-hosted Pages Router app to receive a 500 error instead of a graceful 400. Public DoS PoC available. 3 confirmed reports. This is a clear main-flow failure — every HTTP request to a Server Action endpoint can trigger the crash when Origin is malformed.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker generates incomplete output that breaks pnpm .bin shim creation, causing Docker builds to fail
signals.summary: When running `turbo prune --docker` with pnpm, the pruned output only contains `package.json` files but lacks stub files for binary entries declared in `bin` fields. pnpm refuses to create `.bin` shims without these files, causing subsequent `copy json -> pnpm install -> copy full -> turbo build` sequences to fail during build phases that depend on those shimmed tools.
signals.review_reason: Docker prune is a core CI/CD workflow for turborepo users. The absence of bin stub files causes the pnpm install step in Docker builds to silently skip creating .bin shims, which then causes downstream build tasks to fail with cryptic errors. This is a clear workflow-blocking regression that prevents the documented Docker guide from working for pnpm monorepos.

signals.topic: Child processes (dev servers, tasks) remain orphaned after turbo run receives SIGKILL, incompatible with Playwright and CI tooling
signals.summary: When turbo run receives SIGKILL (e.g., from Playwright test teardown, CI job timeout, or manual `kill -9`), child task processes are not terminated and continue running. This leaves orphaned dev servers and processes consuming ports/resources. Playwright explicitly sends SIGKILL on test close, making turbo unusable in that standard testing setup.
signals.review_reason: SIGKILL is a standard mechanism used by CI timeouts, test frameworks (Playwright, Jest), and container orchestrators to forcibly terminate processes. Turbo not forwarding SIGKILL to child tasks causes resource leaks (orphaned dev servers on ports), test flakiness, and CI pipeline pollution. This blocks the Playwright + Turborepo integration, which is a mainstream CI testing pattern. The user's explicit comparison showing `next dev` works but `turbo run dev` does not confirms this is a turbo-specific regression.

source_issues.title: On SIGKILL to `turbo run`, tasks continue running (incompatible with Playwright testing)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided: run `turbo run dev`, then `kill -9 <turbo_pid>`. The dev server remains running on port 3000. Playwright sends SIGKILL when closing, making turbo unusable with the standard Playwright config. User confirms this does NOT happen when using `next dev` directly instead of `turbo run dev`. Related Playwright issues #33377 and #18209 about Docker SIGKILL behavior.

signals.topic: SIGINT signal not forwarded to underlying task processes, preventing graceful shutdown via Ctrl+C
signals.summary: When a user sends SIGINT (e.g., Ctrl+C) to the turbo process, the signal is not propagated to the child tasks being run. This prevents graceful shutdown of tasks and can result in partial state or lost work, as task processes continue running unaware that the orchestrator has been interrupted.
signals.review_reason: SIGINT (Ctrl+C) is the primary interactive mechanism for developers to interrupt running tasks. Not forwarding SIGINT means tasks cannot perform graceful shutdown (cleanup, flushing buffers, releasing locks), which can lead to corrupted output files, half-written cache entries, or inconsistent state. While less catastrophic than SIGKILL orphaning, this affects every developer who uses turbo interactively and represents a fundamental signal handling contract violation.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` being sent to `turbo` is not forwarded to underlying tasks
source_issues.evidence: Expected behavior: `kill -SIGINT ${TURBO_PID}` should result in SIGINT being sent to all running tasks. Actual behavior: SIGINT is not forwarded. 22 comments indicate sustained user interest and engagement on this issue.

signals.topic: Tasks randomly skipped with no explanation during turbo runs with pnpm, breaking build determinism
signals.summary: When running `turbo tsc` with pnpm in daemon mode, tasks are randomly skipped across runs. The same command sometimes runs all 15 tasks correctly (15 cached) and sometimes runs only a subset (1 cached). Debug logs show incorrect package scoping and wrong task graph hashing on failed runs, indicating a race condition in the package discovery or task graph computation logic.
signals.review_reason: Silent task skipping fundamentally breaks the trust model of a build system. Tasks that users expect to run are silently skipped, and remote cache artifacts from the wrong scope may be returned. This is particularly dangerous because: (1) it is non-deterministic, (2) it produces no error output, (3) remote caching is enabled meaning wrong artifacts may be cached and reused, and (4) it manifests in daemon mode which is the recommended production configuration. The debug logs show the root cause is a package discovery timeout triggering an incorrect fallback strategy.

source_issues.title: Tasks getting skipped with no explanation
source_issues.evidence: User runs `turbo tsc` multiple times consecutively. Some runs produce 15 tasks cached, others produce only 1 task cached. Debug logs show 'primary strategy timed out, attempting fallback strategy' followed by incorrect package scoping (@riptech/app1 instead of @app1/api) and wrong task hash computation. Remote caching is enabled, so skipped tasks are silently served as cached from the wrong scope. This is non-deterministic and breaks build reproducibility.

The user provides a direct comparison (`pnpm -r build` vs `turbo build` on the same codebase) that isolates the issue to turbo's implementation. A profiler trace is available for investigation. This impacts productivity for any developer working on moderately large turborepo monorepos (40+ packages).

Zed hang traces also detected during failure events, indicating possible instability.

signals.topic: Agent run_command tool returns inconsistent or missing stdout for repeated command invocations
signals.summary: The Agent's run_command tool inconsistently returns stdout output. The first invocation of a command may succeed, but subsequent identical invocations return no output at all (no stdout, no stderr, no exit code). The same simple commands (seq 1 10, echo test, ls) reproduce the issue. No error is surfaced when output is missing, making it impossible to distinguish from a valid empty result. The issue is reproducible across Zed restarts and reinstalls.
aliases: Agent command stdout missing on repeat
signals.review_reason: This is a significant Agent workflow degradation. The run_command tool is a core capability of the Agent feature, and its silent failure (no error surfaced, indistinguishable from empty result) makes it unreliable for any real development tasks. The non-deterministic behavior — working once then failing — is particularly insidious as users may not notice until they rely on the output. The app logs also show repeated 'failed to get old checkpoint' errors, suggesting an underlying state management problem in the agent thread subsystem.

source_issues.title: Agent run_command tool returns inconsistent / missing stdout for basic commands
source_issues.evidence: User reports first invocation of run_command returns correct stdout, but subsequent identical invocations return nothing (no stdout, no stderr, no exit code). Reproduction steps show the same trivial commands (seq 1 10, echo test, ls) fail to return output. No error is surfaced, making it indistinguishable from an empty result. Issue persists after Zed restart and reinstall.

signals.topic: Copying Agent input containing code selections pastes the literal word 'selection' and discards all original text; no recovery available
signals.summary: When a user composes a prompt in the Agent input containing code selections (via @file:line references), selecting all text and copying it, then pasting into a new thread, results in all code selections being replaced with the literal word 'selection'. Additionally, once a new thread is started, the previous thread's unsent input is permanently lost with no undo or recovery mechanism. Users lose significant work with no way to retrieve it.
aliases: Agent input copy-paste loses code context
Code selections replaced with word 'selection' on paste
signals.review_reason: This causes direct data loss of user work with no recovery path. While the impact is currently limited to one user's report, the severity is extreme — approximately 1 hour of work (a detailed code review) was permanently lost with no undo, no draft recovery, and no meaningful error message. The copy-paste behavior is also semantically broken: code context is replaced with the word 'selection', defeating the purpose of the feature. This represents a clear and severe user impact.

source_issues.title: Copying prompt with code selections pastes only the word 'selection' and discards original input in the Agent Panel
source_issues.evidence: User spent approximately 1 hour composing a code review across multiple files using code selections in the Agent input. On copy-paste to a new thread, all code selections were replaced by the literal word 'selection', and the original draft was permanently lost. User explicitly states: 'losing roughly an hour of work' with no recovery path.

signals.topic: Devcontainer lifecycle commands (onCreateCommand, updateContentCommand) run as root instead of remoteUser
signals.summary: In devcontainer projects with a non-root remoteUser, the onCreateCommand and updateContentCommand lifecycle commands execute as root (uid=0) instead of the configured remoteUser. This violates the devcontainer specification and causes incorrect behavior in setup scripts that rely on user context. The postCreateCommand and postStartCommand correctly run as the remoteUser.
aliases: remoteUser context not applied to onCreateCommand
signals.review_reason: This is a functional deviation from the devcontainer specification that breaks developer workflows. Two of four lifecycle commands run with the wrong user context, causing setup scripts that check or rely on the current user to fail or produce incorrect results. The root cause is identified: Zed does not pass the remoteUser flag to the Docker exec command for onCreateCommand and updateContentCommand. This is reproducible and the discrepancy is clearly documented in the logs.

source_issues.title: Devcontainer lifecycle commands (onCreateCommand, updateContentCommand) run as root instead of remoteUser
source_issues.evidence: User provides concrete reproduction with a devcontainer JSON specifying remoteUser: 'vscode'. Logs show onCreateCommand: root (uid=0) and updateContentCommand: root (uid=0), while postCreateCommand: vscode (uid=1000) and postStartCommand: vscode (uid=1000) — the latter two are correct. This is a deviation from the devcontainer specification, which requires all lifecycle commands to run as remoteUser.
